BL-132.design:
The fuller co-generation vision deferred from BL-096. Three coupled changes: (1) **population spawns near rich resources** — make generate_population_centres resource-aware; (2) **markets centred on rich trade-route proxies** — since live routes do not exist at gen-time, derive a static resource↔population trade-flow proxy and centre markets on it; (3) **corp-level carving** — place corps before markets (a generation reorder) so competing corporations, not just nations, carve resource clusters. Larger rewrite touching hard_coded_world / nation_generation / market seeding; determinism-sensitive. `requires` BL-096. Authority → GENERATION_STRATEGY.md on landing.

### Settled 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1 procgen review)
**Blocker cleared.** BL-096 (resource-driven market generation) has since shipped — this item's stated dependency is satisfied.

**Sequencing fixed: (1) → (2) → (3), in that order — no reorder.** Population-resource-awareness lands first (a self-contained change to `generate_population_centres`, no reorder of the wider pipeline). The trade-flow proxy lands second, since it reads the now-resource-aware population placement. Corp-level carving lands last, since it's the one genuine generation **reorder** (corps before markets) and should not be entangled with the other two while they're still landing.

**Layer relationship to this sprint's sibling-pass decision (BL-051).** This item operates one layer above tile generation — it's world-seeding order (population → markets → corps), not a tile-generation pass — so the sibling-pass convention doesn't directly apply here; no conflict, just a different extension point. Flipped `design-owed` → `designed`: scope was already well-specified, the blocker is cleared, and sequencing is now fixed.
BL-132.resolution: 2026-08-12 -- complete, delivered as three sequential slices per the item's own settled sequencing (no reorder, not entangled). (1) generate_population_centres weights its candidate pool by nearby extractable-deposit richness (1..5 bucket, multiplicative with the existing 1x/3x adjacency weight), a pure function of generation-time tile data -- no new RNG draw, determinism preserved by construction. (2) A market's centre_tile is now a static resource<->population trade-flow proxy: an 8-tile-radius (wrap-aware) richness/(1+dist^2) gravity search from the anchoring population tile, falling back to the population tile itself when nothing nearby beats it -- live trade routes don't exist at gen-time, so this is the static stand-in the design called for. (3) generate_corporations moved from ~230 lines after Kepler's market-seeding block to just before it (the genuine reorder); the market-carving gate's per-nation concentration term now also multiplies by (1 + corp_presence_gain * distinct-corps-holding-an-asset-in-that-territory), tunable via world_gen.lua's world_gen.kepler_market.carving.corp_presence_gain (default 0.15, 0 = the pre-BL-132 formula) -- a commercially-contested territory fractures further on top of raw geology, layered onto BL-096's existing gate rather than replacing it. BL-141.design:
**Settled — the closed container vocabulary (draft below for Ben's blessing; exact px are his at landing).** The UI is built from a fixed set of containers; every on-screen text/image must live in exactly one. Each is specified by sizing, min/max, text policy, and overflow. Two text policies only: **wrap** (PushTextWrapPos/TextWrapped) or **guaranteed-fit** (measure with CalcTextSize → size the box, the pattern the market-legend key now uses). Images/markers clamp to their container (max-fit).

1. **Fold-out ledger column** (foldout_column) — fixed-width, stretch-to-height, docked to the canvas edge; text **wrap** to inner width; overflow → vertical scroll.
2. **On-canvas lens legend box** (draw-list, body_surface_canvas) — **fit-to-content** (measure → size); text **guaranteed-fit**; no overflow (box grows to fit).
3. **Selection element** (selection_panel) — fixed-width panel (resize pass = BL-123); text **wrap**; overflow → vertical scroll.
4. **Header / balance strip** (header_panel) — stretch-to-width, fixed height; text **guaranteed-fit** (measured segments, never wraps to a second line); overflow → elide-with-tooltip only as a last resort, never silent truncation.
5. **Time panel** (app.cpp) — fixed; text **guaranteed-fit** (authored to fit); no overflow.
6. **Hover card** — fit-to-content with a max width; text **wrap** at max width; overflow → grow vertically.
7. **Minimap lens bar** — fixed strip; icon-only / guaranteed-fit labels; no overflow.
8. **Nav rail** — fixed; icon-only, tooltips wrap.
9. **ImGui table** (ledgers) — stretch columns with min widths; per-cell **guaranteed-fit** (clip + tooltip) or **wrap** for description columns; overflow → horizontal scroll on the table, never silent truncation of load-bearing values.

This lands as a LAYOUT.md section (the authority) and **gates BL-140**, which applies it everywhere. Open (Ben, at landing): confirm the list is complete and set the exact min/max px per container. 2026-07-08 UX review.

BL-146.design:
Follow-on from BL-077 (core). Requires the core's road_level field, per-body grid index, and terrain-weighted A* pathfinder. Runs AFTER nation + population generation (it needs cities to connect) — slots into hard_coded_world.cpp after generate_nations (~line 158).

**Road-generation pass (deterministic from the campaign seed).** Per nation:
1. **Nodes** = the nation's population centres.
2. **Weighted graph** = terrain-weighted A* path cost between each centre-pair (one-off at generation; small node count, not per-Tick).
3. **Backbone = MST + redundancy** — minimum spanning tree over that graph, then a few short extra edges (relative-neighbour rule: keep an edge unless a third centre is closer to both endpoints) for realistic loops. Deterministic tie-break: sort candidate edges by (cost, lower-node-id, higher-node-id).
4. **Two-tier hierarchy** — edges among major centres (City/Metropolis) become **trunk** roads (higher road_level, larger cost cut); spurs linking smaller settlements to their nearest backbone node become **local** roads.
5. **Rasterise** each edge as its terrain-weighted A* path; stamp road_level on the crossed tiles (max on overlap); paths respect the east-west cylinder wrap.
6. **Border links** — after the per-nation networks exist, add one link between the nearest city-pair across each adjacent-nation boundary, so the continent-wide lattice is connected.

Cities enumerable via world.population_centres + population_centre_tile. New TU road_generation.{hpp,cpp} keeps the pass off the tile_generation hotspot; wired in hard_coded_world.cpp (main-session integration). Determinism guard: add road_level to the determinism_harness field checks.

**Tuning (settle at promotion):** trunk/local road_level values and their A* cost-cut. **Authority:** SUPPLY.md (road cost-reducer) + TILE_GENERATION.md (the generation pass).
BL-146.completion_note: Landed 2026-07-10. New src/world/road_generation.{hpp,cpp}: generate_roads(w, body) runs in hard_coded_world.cpp after generate_nations, deterministically stamping tile.road_level. Per nation over its population centres: pairwise terrain-weighted A* (intra_body_path) costs, Kruskal MST tie-broken by (cost, lo-tile-id, hi-tile-id), plus relative-neighbour redundancy edges; trunk (road_level 2) between major centres (scale>=3) else local (1); rasterised along the A* path taking max road_level and skipping ocean. Then one local border link between the nearest centre pair of each territorially-adjacent nation pair (4-cardinal + column-wrap adjacency scan). Clears world.astar_cost_cache at the end (roads were measured road-free for the MST, so the cache is stale after stamping) per the world.hpp invalidation contract. Tuning settled with Ben: local=1/trunk=2, major=scale>=3. Verified headless via tools/verify/road_generation_harness.cpp: R1 lattice exists + no ocean roads, R2 both tiers present + none exceed trunk, R3 14/14 non-isolated centres touch a road, R4 road_level identical across two generations (determinism). Regression: determinism/logistics/trade_routes/econ/world_audit harnesses all green. Authority propagated to SUPPLY.md + TILE_GENERATION.md. BL-150.design:
**Problem.** The commercial-activity fog (BL-089, `body_activity_visibility` -> Solar badges in `solar_system_canvas.cpp:249`) is a presence-badge on LIT bodies, not an overlay on the dark. Unknown bodies draw nothing, so the fog is invisible until the player runs commerce, and the small lower-left pulse dots are easily lost. Prompted by Ben 2026-07-08 ('I'm not seeing any fog').

**Change.** Render the activity fog as a **dim shadow**: bodies the player's commercial network does NOT reach are drawn dimmed/shadowed on the Solar canvas (a translucent dark wash and/or reduced body+label brightness), so the un-networked map legibly reads as *fogged*; as a route/convoy reaches a body it **brightens** to full (known -> visible a rising brightness ramp). The existing lower-left pulse badge can stay as the fine-grained tier tell for the lit tiers; the shadow is the new coarse read for the unlit. Keep it visually distinct from the geographic **survey** fog (BL-067, the '?' badges) — the two fogs must still read apart (DISCOVERY.md's two-independent-fogs rule).

**Scope.** Solar canvas only (the activity fog is body-level). Home stays full-bright (its BL-085 halo). Derived read only — no new sim state (reads `body_activity_visibility`). `presentation.hpp/.cpp` for the shadow colour/alpha + brightness ramp; `solar_system_canvas.cpp` for the per-body dim.

BL-150.summary: Filed 2026-07-08 (Ben) after observing the commercial-activity fog reads as 'no fog'. Today (BL-089) the activity fog is ABSENCE-by-default: an unknown body draws nothing (a plain astronomy dot); only known/known_stale/visible non-home bodies get a small ~4-6px lower-left pulse badge. So with no player commerce the whole Solar map looks identical to no-fog, and even when lit the badges are subtle next to the survey '?' + labels. This item inverts the treatment: render the fog as a DIM SHADOW over bodies outside the player's commercial network, so the unlit map READS as fogged and brightens as commerce reaches it.

BL-151.design:
**Semantics (Ben's call).** Commercial reach, not unknown-terrain: the home planet is the player's own territory, so 'fog' means *where your logistics actually operate*. **Substrate (Ben's call).** Live-derived, no stored state / no save-format change; intra-body traffic records nothing persistent.

**Model.** Vision is a TIGHT pocket around the player's actual presence, not a whole market catchment (a first cut lit the entire catchment — Ben: 'too wide'; the point is a sense of movement + unknowns). Reveal sources: the player's own building tiles + the endpoint (`centre_tile`) of any live player convoy on the active body. A breadth-first flood out to `fog_reveal_radius` (=3) tile-hops from every source marks the visible pocket (odd-r offset neighbours, column wrap); every other revealed tile takes a dark wash (`lerp 0.5` toward IM_COL32(8,10,16)). Applied over the lens fill (a fogged region's analytic read dims with it). The geographic survey fog (BL-067) still owns unrevealed tiles — this dims revealed ones only. Always-on, all overlays. Convoys confirmed live (dispatch/advance/credit run every econ step, app.cpp:381).

**Verify.** `scripts/verify/intrabody_fog.lua` (goto_surface home + zoom-out capture). Probe at landing: home body 7 markets, player reaches 1 -> 6 catchments fogged; tightened to radius pockets so the HQ region reads lit and the rest of the globe fogged at both play and wide zoom.

**Follow-up -> BL-152:** a live convoy should emit a radius-2 vision BEAM that travels its route and lags/dims over ~1 econ tick (needs `logistics_path` to return its tile sequence — currently cost-only). That is the 'things are moving' half; this item is the static-presence half.
BL-151.summary: Filed + landed 2026-07-09 (Ben, follow-on from BL-150). The commercial-activity fog (BL-089) is body-level only, rendered on the Solar canvas; the Planetary canvas had no activity fog, so the home surface read as fully known. Ben expected fog of war on the home planet over intra-body trade. This adds a THIRD visibility treatment: a per-tile intra-body fog on the Planetary canvas so the surface reads as mostly unknown, lit only around the player's own presence.

BL-152.design:
**Spec (Ben).** 'Convoys should send a radius 2 beam of vision which lags and dims over 1 econ tick.'

**Path exposure.** `logistics_path` (world.hpp) gained a `tiles` sequence; `intra_body_path` (logistics.cpp) reconstructs it via a came_from parent-walk, stored in canonical lo->hi endpoint order (the route cache is keyed on the unordered pair). Deterministic; wrap-aware (the grid is a horizontal cylinder). Verified by a throwaway headless probe (contiguity, canonical order, single-tile src==dst).

**Vision buffer.** `ui_state.convoy_vision` maps tile -> the sim time (elapsed days) a beam last lit it; `ui_state.sim_now_days` is the continuous fade clock (set every frame in app.cpp). Derived VIEW state only — never serialised, no feedback into world/*, so world determinism is preserved (a `world/*` standing rule).

**Refresh (per econ step).** `ui::update_convoy_vision` (body_surface_canvas) runs in app::step_economy after advance_convoys (before arrived convoys are retired). For each live player intra-body convoy it maps progress -> a path-index segment (where it was one tick ago .. now), floods radius-2 (odd-r neighbours) around that segment, and stamps now_days. Prunes entries older than one econ tick.

**Render.** The Planetary fog (BL-151) now blends a beam vision term: vision = 1 in the static pocket, else max with the beam's fading contribution (1 - age/90); fog wash = 0.5*(1 - vision). So a convoy's beam trails and dims behind it over one econ tick. Uses continuous sim time, so it fades smoothly between quarter boundaries rather than snapping.

**Scope note.** Intra-body convoys only (inter-body activity reads on the Solar fog, BL-089/150). econ_tick_days (90) mirrored as a local constant in the canvas to avoid a ui->core include. **Authority:** docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md.

**Superseded 2026-07-09 by BL-154:** the per-econ-step segment-flood + timestamp-fade was replaced by a render-time moving head/tail beam (interpolated by econ-tick fraction) + permanent corp-centre->market corridors. The path-exposure work here stands; the buffer/refresh mechanism was reworked.
BL-152.summary: Filed + landed 2026-07-09 (Ben, the 'things are moving' half of BL-151). A live player convoy emits a radius-2 beam of vision along the tiles it moves through; that vision lags and dims over one econ tick (90 days). The moving-presence complement to BL-151's static-presence pocket.

BL-154.design:
**Change 1 — moving head/tail beam.** The BL-152 buffer (per-econ-step segment flood, uniform timestamp fade) read as a chunky blob that stepped once per quarter. Replaced with a RENDER-TIME moving beam: `ui_state.convoy_beams` stores each live player intra-body convoy's tile path + progress + speed (rebuilt each frame in `update_body_vision`); the canvas interpolates a HEAD along the path by the fraction through the current econ tick (`fmod(sim_now_days,90)/90`), so it glides smoothly between quarterly steps, and trails a TAIL one econ tick's travel behind, ramping intensity 1->0 head->tail, radius-2 around each path tile. So the beam has a bright moving head and a dimming tail.

**Change 2 — permanent corp-centre->market corridors (Ben: 'from the corp centre of operation to the market centre, as a 3 wide beam').** `ui_state.permanent_vision` (non-fading) = radius-2 pockets around the player's own building tiles + 3-wide corridors (path flooded radius 1) from the corp centre of operation (lowest-id player building tile on the body, mirroring market_clearing's file-local representative_tile) to each market centre the player operates in (the catchment markets of its buildings). Always visible.

**Plumbing.** `update_body_vision` (renamed from update_convoy_vision) rebuilds both buffers per frame for the active body; moved from app::step_economy to render() (planetary branch) so the --verify capture path gets it too, and so a body switch is tracked immediately. Pathfinder is route-cache-backed (steady-state = lookups). Derived VIEW state only — no serialisation, no world/* feedback; determinism preserved.

**Render.** Fog vision = 1 in permanent_vision, else the moving beam's intensity; wash = 0.5*(1 - vision). Verified: full build clean; wide + default captures show permanent pockets/corridors lit and the globe fogged (the moving beam's motion only manifests with a live inter-market intra-body convoy, not the same-market verify seed). **Authority:** docs/ui/DISCOVERY.md.

Two changes to the intra-body vision model: (1) the convoy beam should MOVE with a head and tail that update (not a uniformly-fading segment); (2) permanent vision as a 3-wide beam from the corp centre of operation to the market centre. Reworks the vision buffers accordingly.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the minimum stub, and the force that is deliberately absent


### Sequencing note — this was deliberately deferred, and is being settled anyway

Sprint 2 (2026-07-31) records Ben's call to sequence BL-210's nation rewrite *first*, because
designing policy/military/politics against nations that BL-218 is about to stop being Voronoi
blobs risks rework. That reasoning still holds and is not overturned here.

Settled now on Ben's 2026-08-02 instruction to work through the design-owed set regardless of
deferral, in preparation for a batch delivery. **The rework exposure is real but bounded**, and
bounding it is a design constraint rather than a footnote: everything below is specified against
*nation identity and nation-owned state*, never against how a nation's territory or character was
DERIVED. BL-218 changes the derivation (simulated settlement history in place of Voronoi + a
random politics draw); it does not change that a nation has an id, territory, a character and
relationships. Any part of these designs that would break under BL-218 is a part that reached
into generation, and none of them do.

This item had no design at all beyond its scope statement. Settling it against its own hardest
constraint: "the minimum stub that earns its place without inviting scope creep."

### There is no `force` record. A unit with an owner and a position is the whole footing.

The item names "units, forces" as though both are needed. **Only the unit is.** A force is an
*aggregation* of units — it can be derived by grouping on (owner, position) whenever something
needs it, and nothing needs it yet because there is no movement, no combat and no AI.

Adding a `force` record now would mean inventing a grouping rule with no consumer to validate
it against, then serialising it, then keeping it consistent with unit membership across every
future mutation. That is three obligations bought for zero present value, and it is exactly the
scope creep the item warns against. **Derive it later, when something asks.**

### The unit record

Stored the way every other entity is — an id-keyed map beside `world::buildings`, so it
inherits the existing entity, serialisation and selection conventions rather than inventing
parallel ones:

- **`id`** — entity id.
- **`owner`** — a nation or corporation id. Note this is deliberately *either*: BL-094 gives
  military to the nation, but corporate security forces are within the game's premise, and a
  field that admits both costs nothing now and avoids a migration later.
- **`position`** — a tile id, reusing the existing tile entity. Not a coordinate pair; tiles
  already carry body membership, terrain and adjacency, all of which any future movement or
  combat rule will want.
- **`type`** — an enum with a small authored set, mirroring `building_type`.
- **`strength`** — one fixed-point scalar. Not a stat block. A single scalar is enough to
  prove the record serialises and renders, and a stat block is a mechanics decision that
  Conflict-proper owns.

### The seam that already exists, and is the reason this is cheap

**`selection_kind::unit` is already in `selection_panel.cpp`** — the Selection element already
has a unit case, currently unreachable because nothing constructs a unit. So the stub's
acceptance check is concrete and needs no new UI: **generate one unit, select it, and see the
Selection element resolve it.** That is a real end-to-end proof of the record (existence,
ownership, position, render, serialisation round-trip) without a single line of mechanics.

Terrain combat modifiers (BL-233) are already **complete**, so the terrain half of a future
combat rule exists and has no units to apply to. This stub is the other half of that seam.

### Explicitly not in scope

Movement, combat resolution, stacking rules, supply, unit production or cost, any AI, and any
force aggregation. If a design question needs one of those to answer it, the question belongs
to Conflict-proper (TECH_FOUNDATIONS exclusions), not here.

## Military design session rulings (2026-08-07, Ben)

- **Tile position ruled canonical** (over body and over province). The shipped `unit_component` in components.hpp still carries `body` — that divergence (half the record landed under BL-272 with a different position model) is fixed as part of landing this item: `position` becomes a tile id, `strength` scalar added, `type` indexes UNITS.json’s roster when BL-274 lands.
- **Verbs act at UNIT grain** (BL-314): no force record, consistent with this item’s no-force settlement. The order-volume concern (many march orders per tick) is accepted; if it bites, a derived-force grouping is the fallback and gets designed then, not now.
- The Era −1 sim reads provinces; the projection from tile to province is the sim’s job, not a second position field.

## RESOLUTION (2026-08-08)

The record stub landed as part of BL-324 (unit hire surface): `unit_component.position` is now
a tile id (the `body` field it shipped with was the divergence this item always meant to fix at
landing), plus a fixed-point `strength` scalar; `world::units` is the id-keyed map beside
`world::buildings`. The acceptance check this item named — select a unit, see the Selection
element resolve it — is now genuinely reachable via BL-324's hire affordance, not just proven by
a hand-seeded stub. The hybrid-unit/zone-of-control/multi-round-battle design thread below stays
OPEN — it is scoped beyond this stub (Conflict mechanics proper), not a blocker on it.

## Design thread — hybrid units, zone of control, multi-round battles (2026-08-07, open — Ben to react)

Ben's steer: pad out unit variety with **hybrid-type units**, give a unit a **zone of control** wider than the one tile it occupies (5–8 tiles), and stop resolving battles instantly — run them over a while with random events, keeping the math simple. Rendering is explicitly undecided; three sketches were produced to react to, not a chosen direction. None of this is settled — recorded here so it isn't lost, not as a ruling.

### Hybrid units — lean: blended roster entries, not a composite/force model

BL-272's `resolve_battle` already keys off a `unit_class` matchup matrix (infantry/cavalry/ranged/siege/naval) plus a per-type `type_power_mod`. A hybrid unit is cheapest as a **roster entry with a blended class weight** — e.g. a "combined cohort" type carrying a 60/40 infantry/ranged profile that the matchup math averages across — rather than compositing several sub-units under one id. The latter would reopen this item's own "no force record, unit grain" settlement (and BL-314's verbs-act-at-unit-grain ruling) for no real gain. Blended weighting is pure roster data for BL-274 (era-keyed rosters); it needs no engine change. RTS precedent: Total War's legion cohorts, Wargame's combined-arms battlegroups — the flavour comes from the mix ratio, not from tracking sub-units separately.

### Zone of control — a radius-1 footprint over the unit's tile neighbourhood

Classic hex-wargame ZOC, and a natural fit for Io's tile-adjacency model: `position` stays the one canonical tile (already ruled above), but a unit **projects control** over its neighbourhood — a radius-1 footprint is 7 tiles on hex, 9 on square-with-diagonals, in the 5–8 range Ben named. **Open question, deliberately not settled:** does ZOC deny enemy building placement, interdict convoys passing through, feed the DISCOVERY.md activity-fog visibility tiers, or some mix of the three? Worth reusing the **terrain-weighted reach query** the v0.1.2 buildings rework (BL-323) is about to build for logistical placement range, rather than the two efforts inventing parallel range math — flag this for whoever lands ZOC.

### Multi-round battles — a bounded outer loop around the existing resolver, not a replacement for it

BL-272's `resolve_battle` is deliberately **one** deterministic evaluation, because the Era −1 sweep (BL-271/275) needs to run millions of engagements cheaply — that constraint does not move. But nothing stops a **small, fixed-round outer loop** wrapping it for the main era: N rounds (bounded, e.g. 3–6), each round re-calling `resolve_battle` with attrition/morale carried forward from the prior round, plus a **seeded** event roll per round (reinforcement arrives, weather flips the season modifier, a rout). Shape matches EU4/CK2-style land battles — daily rounds, morale break, the occasional flavour event — and keeps the arithmetic as simple as the existing per-mille math. Hard constraint, not optional: the event RNG must be seeded off battle id + round, never wall-clock (io-standing-rules § Determinism). The file header's "cost must not scale with battlefield size" ban likely survives a *fixed* round count, since it scales with rounds, not size — but that reading is not yet verified against BL-271's actual sweep cost budget.

### Rendering — undecided, three sketches produced to react to

No direction chosen. Three candidate treatments were sketched in the same session: (1) an on-canvas contested-tile glyph with a low-alpha ZOC wash over the neighbourhood, in the existing ICONS.md stroke-only convention; (2) a Conflict Ledger entry mirroring the Market/Balance/Construction ledger family, one row per active battle with a power bar and latest event line; (3) a drill-through battle-detail panel (two-column force readout + round-by-round event log) opened from either. They compose — (1) is the map-level signal, (3) is what it opens into, (2) is a middle ground for tracking several simultaneous battles without hunting the map. Whoever designs this properly should treat all three as a menu, not assume (3) is the only one that ships.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — most of this item was already dissolved; what is left is the relationship axis


### Sequencing note — this was deliberately deferred, and is being settled anyway

Sprint 2 (2026-07-31) records Ben's call to sequence BL-210's nation rewrite *first*, because
designing policy/military/politics against nations that BL-218 is about to stop being Voronoi
blobs risks rework. That reasoning still holds and is not overturned here.

Settled now on Ben's 2026-08-02 instruction to work through the design-owed set regardless of
deferral, in preparation for a batch delivery. **The rework exposure is real but bounded**, and
bounding it is a design constraint rather than a footnote: everything below is specified against
*nation identity and nation-owned state*, never against how a nation's territory or character was
DERIVED. BL-218 changes the derivation (simulated settlement history in place of Voronoi + a
random politics draw); it does not change that a nation has an id, territory, a character and
relationships. Any part of these designs that would break under BL-218 is a part that reached
into generation, and none of them do.

### BL-155 already removed the larger half

The politics-is-laws framing settled 2026-07-11 (BL-155 § Politics ~ laws) means a nation's
**political character is a named law-bundle preset** — a Laws *consumer*, not a new object. A
protectionist nation is high tariffs plus export duties; a laissez-faire one is near-zero
extraction tax and no emissions levy.

So the economic-behaviour half of a political profile needs **no schema of its own**: it is a
preset id plus the law records it expands to. This item inherits that (its own field now updated,
per the authority time-slice rule) and what remains is genuinely one thing.

### The relationship axis: ASYMMETRIC per-pair sentiment

The one piece of political state that is not a law, because a diplomacy state is not a modifier
over a flow.

**Asymmetric — `sentiment[from][to]`, not a symmetric pair value.** Symmetric is half the
storage and is the wrong model, for a reason that already exists in the backlog: **BL-225**
(asset seizure costs the seizing nation sentiment and credit access) is inherently
*directional*. A nation that seizes assets loses standing **with the observers**, and each
observer's reaction differs by how exposed it was. A symmetric scalar cannot express "A resents
B, B is indifferent", which is the ordinary case in the averted-rupture premise (BL-223) the
history ladder produces.

The stub is therefore:

- **`sentiment`** — a fixed-point scalar per ordered pair, one bounded range, no sub-axes.
  (Trust/fear/respect decomposition is a v0.3.0 question; one axis proves the storage.)
- **`character_preset`** — a preset id per nation, expanding to law records via BL-155.
- **No lever slots.** The original scope names "placeholder lever slots"; those are laws, and
  BL-155 owns them. A placeholder for a thing that already has a home is a future
  reconciliation problem.

### Determinism

An N-by-N table over nations, and the default seed now generates **43** of them (up from 14 at
v0.0.3, since BL-221 landed). That is ~1,850 ordered pairs — trivial for storage, but it makes
the walk rule load-bearing rather than pedantic: **any iteration over pairs is a sorted walk
over nation ids**, never over an unordered container, and any aggregate (a nation's average
standing) accumulates in fixed point in that fixed order. This is the same rule as BL-222's
first-industrialiser argmax, and at 43 nations it is the kind of thing that produces a
seed-dependent divergence nobody can reproduce.

### Sizing

Difficulty stays 2. Half the item dissolved into BL-155 and what remains is one table and one
preset id — but it is now correctly the *last* of the four stubs, since it consumes BL-155's
law records and cannot be specified before them.

BL-162.design:
## BL-162 — Tile construction ledger: the per-candidate expected-profit chart

### Status of the existing surface (verified 2026-07-30 against the code)

The backlog's original prose — "the construction entry point cannot build" — is **stale and
superseded**. `ui::draw_construction_ledger` (`src/ui/selection_panel.cpp:1265`, declared
`selection_panel.hpp:70`, drawn from `app.cpp:2666`) already works end to end:

- enumerates candidates (`:1323-1332`) — one extraction row per extractable resource actually
  deposited on the tile, then Processing Facility / Port / Launchpad / Inland Logistics Hub, plus
  a separate three-tier road block (`:1398-1475`);
- prints full cost, credits then materials (`:1364-1369`);
- prints a reason-coded validity read from `placement_rules::can_place_in_world` (`:1342`, `:1390`);
- has a Build action that genuinely enqueues via `ui.construction.pending_tile/type/target`
  (`:1375-1380`), drained by `app.cpp:2675-2705` into the real `construct_building`.

`docs/ui/SELECTION.md` is correct. **Nothing above is redesigned or rebuilt.** The one placeholder
is the 56x56 grey box at `:1350-1357` (and its road twin at `:1430-1436`).

### What this item delivers

Replace the placeholder image with a **per-candidate expected-profit read**: every buildable
candidate carries a horizontal magnitude bar, drawn on a **ceiling shared across the whole list**,
so the player can rank the options on this tile at a glance and sorted so the best five are the
five on screen. Two adjacent defects that the chart makes intolerable are fixed in the same pass
(a lying affordability gate; the ledger closing itself on every build).

---

### 1. The prospective estimator (the seam)

`estimate_building_profit` **cannot** be used. It hard-requires an existing `building_component`
(`building_profit.cpp:14-17`) *and* a matching `report.buildings` row (`:20-24`), and its revenue is
`br->output_quantity` — a realised figure, not a model. Both miss on an empty tile.

Add a sibling to `src/world/building_profit.{hpp,cpp}`, returning the **same `building_profit`
struct** so a candidate's numbers read identically to a built building's:

```cpp
/// Expected per-tick unit economics of a building that does NOT yet exist, on `tile_id`.
/// Pure read of `world` + `registry` — no economy_report, no RNG, no caches.
building_profit estimate_prospective_profit(const world& w, const recipe_registry& reg,
                                            entity_id tile_id, building_type type,
                                            resource_type target,
                                            std::uint16_t recipe_id = no_recipe);
```

Model, fixed and explicit:

| Term | Value | Mirrors |
|---|---|---|
| `workforce_assigned` | `0.5f`, or `0.0f` for `port` / `inland_logistics_hub` | `construction.cpp:84-85` |
| `workforce_target` | `100` | `building_component`'s default |
| contention scalar | `1.0f` (no economy_report; assume no labour shortage) | stated in the caption |
| habitability | `body_mean_habitability(w, body)` | `apply_budget` exactly |
| `maintenance`, `wages` | `compute_building_opex(synthetic_bc, reg.economics(type), 1.0f, hab)` | exact budget parity |
| extraction revenue | `base_rate * tc.resource_deposit[target] * wf * (1 - tc.hazard_level) * price(target)` | `economy_system.cpp:71`, `wt_scalar = 1` |
| processing | `batches = base_rate * wf`; revenue `= Σ outputs[r]*batches*price(r)`; `input_cost = Σ inputs[r]*batches*price(r)` | `run_processing` |
| port / launchpad / hub | `revenue = 0`, `input_cost = 0` | they produce nothing |

`price(r)` is the tile's market: `market_for_tile(w, tile_id)` → `price[r] > 0 ? price[r] :
base_price[r]` (the `local_price` shape from `corp_ai.cpp:35`; keep it file-local in
`building_profit.cpp`). `has_data = false` when the tile is missing **or** no market resolves — a
chart of zeros is a lie.

**Deliberately not modelled** (do not "improve" these):
- **Price response.** No supply-shift elasticity; today's prices, flat. `solve_workforce_target`'s
  `wf_target_price` is not reused — a half-modelled elasticity is less legible than an honestly
  captioned static one.
- **Deposit sharing.** `run_extraction` gives every building the full `tc.resource_deposit[ri]`;
  a second site on the same deposit really does get the same richness. No adjustment.
- **Depletion taper.** A function of extracted-to-date, which is zero for a building that does not
  exist.

`corp_ai.cpp:239-249` keeps its inline crude duplicate (it omits habitability-scaled wages).
Switching it would change AI build scoring, hence world evolution, hence every blessed golden.
Known accepted divergence; add a comment pointing at the new function, change no behaviour.

### 2. Candidate model — one row per (type, target, recipe)

`processing_facility` expands into **one row per recipe** (`reg.recipe_count(processing_facility)`
= 3: steel, refined fuel, food rations). Their margins genuinely diverge, and `construct_building`
today hard-codes `reg.recipe_id("steel")` — so a single type-level bar priced at steel would report
"processing loses money here" while food rations is strongly profitable on the same tile. That is a
load-bearing figure silently misreporting.

The recipe therefore has to survive to construction. Seam, all additive and defaulted so no existing
caller changes:

- `ui_state::construction_state` gains `std::uint16_t pending_recipe = no_recipe;`
- `construct_building(...)` gains a trailing `std::uint16_t recipe = no_recipe`; where it sets
  `bc.recipe = reg.recipe_id("steel")` it becomes
  `bc.recipe = (recipe != no_recipe) ? recipe : reg.recipe_id("steel");`
- `app.cpp`'s pending drain passes it and clears it to `no_recipe` alongside `pending_tile`.

No save-format change: `building_component.recipe` is already serialised.

Row names must stay unique (the card's ImGui id is `c.name`): `"Processing: Steel"`,
`"Processing: Refined Fuel"`, `"Processing: Food Rations"` via a file-local `pretty_recipe()`
(underscores to spaces, title-case).

### 3. Row anatomy — the placeholder image is removed, not re-skinned

The 56x56 grey box is **deleted**. `charts::gutter` (40) alone exceeds it; nothing chart-like fits
there. Its 56 + 8 px of width is reclaimed by the row, which the column badly needs. Building
identity survives as an **18 px inline `icons::building` glyph** before the name.

Four lines per candidate card, at 278 px inner width (see § 4):

1. **Name** — 18 px glyph, then the name in `palette::selection`.
2. **Cost** — `TextDisabled`, credits **including material cost priced at the local market**, then,
   only when net > 0, ` · payback ~<n> ticks` (`capex / net`, `capex = build_cost + material_cost`;
   print `payback > 999 ticks` above that).
3. **Profit bar row**, 14 px tall — one of exactly three states:
   - *valid producing candidate*: `charts::draw_value_bar`, colour `palette::positive` /
     `palette::negative` / `palette::neutral` by sign of `net()`;
   - *valid non-producing* (Port, Launchpad, Inland Logistics Hub): no bar,
     `palette::neutral` text `"Infrastructure - no direct revenue; upkeep %.0f / tick"`;
   - *invalid candidate, or `has_data == false`*: no bar — the row's reason text occupies this slot.
4. **Action** — Build button (disabled + "Can't afford" when unaffordable) or the red
   `pr.message()`, exactly as today.

Roads keep their existing three-tier block unchanged and get **no** profit row (a road is a tile
mutation with no `building_component` and no upkeep in the model). Their placeholder box keeps its
tier-weighted line glyph; only their affordability gate is fixed.

**Sign encoding.** `charts::draw_bars`' `y_of(v)` inverts the rect for negative values and would
draw outside the clip box — a rendering bug, not a style choice. So bar **length encodes magnitude**
(`|net| / ceiling`), **colour encodes sign**, and the **signed value is printed in full**,
right-aligned, never elided. Because the list is sorted net-descending, every green sits above every
red, so the sign is obvious from position too.

**Shared ceiling** = `charts::tight_ceil(max |net|)` over the **valid producing candidates only**.
Invalid and infrastructure rows are excluded so they cannot inflate the axis and squash the bars
that matter. `tight_ceil` (not `nice_ceil`) keeps the tallest bar above ~70 % of the track.

**Caption**, once, above the list, `TextWrapped` in `palette::text_dim`:
`"Est. net / tick at today's local prices - 50% staffing, no labour shortage. Capex is not in the bar; see payback."`

### 4. Geometry — measured, not chosen

`charts::draw_bars` **cannot be used here**, and this is arithmetic rather than preference:

```
foldout_column_rect().w  = shell_column_width(disp.x) - nav_pane_width = 380 - 56 = 324   (the floor)
  - window WindowPadding 2x8                                                     = 308
  - ##build_list AlwaysVerticalScrollbar (ScrollbarSize 14)                      = 294
  - candidate card BeginChild(border=true) WindowPadding 2x8                     = 278   <- the design width
draw_bars: band = max(60, 278 - gutter(40) - legend_w(190)) = 60
```

60 px of plot for every column and gap. At 3+ bars it degenerates to 6 px stubs overflowing into
the legend — which is exactly why the tile accordion only ever passes two. Hand-rolling a bar in
`selection_panel.cpp` would break the "reuse the idiom" rule, so **extend `charts.{hpp,cpp}`** with
the primitive a narrow list actually needs. Per the Save-the-tool rule it then *is* the idiom
(BL-176's building table wants the same shape):

```cpp
/// One horizontal magnitude bar inside [mn, mx], for a narrow list where a clustered
/// vertical chart cannot fit (draw_bars reserves gutter + a 190px legend, exceeding the
/// fold-out column's ~278px row width). Length = |value| / ceiling; colour is the caller's;
/// the signed value prints right-aligned and is NEVER elided.
void draw_value_bar(ImDrawList* dl, ImVec2 mn, ImVec2 mx,
                    float value, float ceiling, ImU32 colour, const char* fmt = "%+.0f");
```

Internals: track `AddRectFilled(mn, mx, IM_COL32(48,50,58,255), 2.0f)`; value text measured with
`CalcTextSize`, `plot_w = (mx.x - mn.x) - std::max(52.0f, text_w) - 6.0f`; fill
`AddRectFilled({mn.x, mn.y}, {mn.x + plot_w * clamp(|value|/ceiling, 0, 1), mx.y}, colour, 2.0f)`;
a 2 px stub at the origin when `value == 0` or `ceiling <= 0` so zero reads as zero rather than as
absent; text right-aligned at `mx.x - text_w`, vertically centred, `IM_COL32(225,228,235,255)`.
Reserving `max(52, text_w)` means the figure can never be truncated **or** collide with the bar.

Row height, from the ImGui default style (`FramePadding {4,3}`, `ItemSpacing {4,4}`,
`WindowPadding {8,8}`):

```cpp
constexpr float bar_h = 14.0f;
const float row_h = style.WindowPadding.y * 2.0f
                  + ImGui::GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing()   // name
                  + ImGui::GetTextLineHeightWithSpacing()   // cost + payback
                  + bar_h + style.ItemSpacing.y             // profit bar
                  + ImGui::GetFrameHeight();                // Build / reason
```

≈ **87 px** (vs today's 80), pitch ≈ 95 px with the trailing `Spacing()`.

**Rows before scrolling.** Ledger height at 720 = `disp.y - profile_panel_height` = 628; header
block (title row 23 + separator 9 + Balance 17 + toast 17 + wrapped caption 30 + padding 16) ≈ 112;
list ≈ 516 → **5 rows fully visible, the 6th partial**. All 13 (4 extraction + 3 processing + 3
infrastructure + 3 road) fit by ~1150 px of display height. `##build_list` already carries
`AlwaysVerticalScrollbar` — keep it. Widths scale with `shell_column_width` (324 at the 380 floor
through 1900 px wide, 328 at 1920, 404 at the 460 cap); nothing is hard-coded to 324.

### 5. Sort order — confirmed, with a deterministic tail

`std::stable_sort` over the candidate vector, ties falling back to declaration order:

1. valid **producing** candidates, expected `net()` **descending**;
2. valid **infrastructure** (Port, Launchpad, Inland Logistics Hub), declaration order;
3. **invalid** candidates, declaration order;
4. **roads**, unchanged, in their own block after the list.

With recipe expansion the list is two screens deep at 720p, so the sort is what makes it usable —
the best five are the five you see without scrolling. `stable_sort` plus declaration-order ties
keeps the order frame-stable and free of any `unordered_map` iteration dependence.

### 6. Two defects fixed in the same pass

**(a) The affordability gate lies.** `selection_panel.cpp:1344` gates on `econ.build_cost` alone;
`construction.cpp:72` gates on `build_cost + material_cost`. Between those two figures the ledger
shows an **enabled** Build button that fails, with only a post-hoc toast, and materials print in raw
units the player cannot price. Mirror `construction.cpp:50-67`'s material sum, gate on the total,
and print the cost line as a **credit total**. Same fix on the road path (`:1424` vs
`construction.cpp:176-178`). Putting a precise profit bar next to a lying capex figure is worse than
either alone — and `payback` needs the true capex anyway.

**(b) A successful build closes the ledger.** `app.cpp:2690-2691` reassigns
`m_ui.selected_entity = built`, the selection stops being a tile, and `app.cpp:2665-2668` forces
`show_build_ledger = false`. Suppress that reassignment **when `m_ui.show_build_ledger` is true**
(canvas placement keeps its current behaviour). A rich tile stacks up to 4 extraction sites; a
comparison chart for one tile must survive a build. It also makes "Construction started." — written
to `ui.construction.last_message` and drawn at `selection_panel.cpp:1316` *inside the ledger that
just closed* — finally visible, and lets the chart re-evaluate against the newly occupied slot.

- **Container vocabulary.** No tenth container. The ledger is container 1, *Fold-out ledger column*

  The profit value is load-bearing and reserves its own measured width — never silently truncated.
- **Determinism.** `estimate_prospective_profit` is a pure read of `world` + `recipe_registry`; no

  quantity must read identically before and after the build.
- **Trade.** The item's justification: it converts "here are things you may build" into "here is
  what each would earn", which is the decision that seeds every later trade the building feeds.

**Idea — design owed.** Today agriculture is a single terrain-affinity extraction (RESOURCES.md / PRODUCTION.md). The proposal: farming that feeds population where terrestrial affinities (arable land, water/river adjacency, climate) are absent should be a distinct recipe/building — a controlled-environment / hydroponic food building consuming refined inputs (energy, water, structural goods) rather than raw terrain. BL-167.design:
**Idea — parked, design owed (original framing).** Tile generation already derives static solar parameters per body (temperature class, atmosphere class, hydrological state, geological activity — TILE_GENERATION.md) and bands oceans by a noise height field. This idea originally proposed a climate model: latitude/altitude-driven temperature and moisture bands. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

### Re-settled 2026-07-21 (Ben, Sprint 1 procgen review) — supersedes the original 'climate modelling' framing
**Reframed as Planetology: a body-level history/chemistry pass, not just a tile-level climate band.** Ben's explicit reference is **Shadow Empire's** planet generation (VR Designs/Slitherine) — researched this session. Shadow Empire generates each world through three phases: **Planetology** (astrophysical rolls — age, gravity, temperature, water retention, initial atmosphere composition), **Geology** (terrain/rainfall derived from the Planetology rolls), and a simulated **Evolution** phase (hundreds of millions of years of abiogenesis-gated biological history, listing any species that arose and went extinct before colonisation). Atmospheric composition is explicitly **impacted by the emergence of life** — a planet with a thriving biosphere reads ~15% oxygen; a planet where abiogenesis conditions were never met keeps a sterile, thinner atmosphere and may lack fossil fuels entirely. This is the model Ben wants Project Io's body generation to work toward, because — his words — it's 'the first thing a player sees' and has to carry real first-impression weight.

**Scope for this item:**
1. **Initial atmosphere generation** — derive a per-body atmosphere composition (gas mix, not just the current single `atmosphere_class` enum) from basic chemistry: the body's solar parameters (temperature class, geological activity, water retention) set the starting inorganic mix (CO2/N2/H2O vapour/trace gases), same spirit as Shadow Empire's Planetology roll.
2. **A simulated abiogenesis/evolution pass** — gate life's emergence on chemistry preconditions (liquid water, temperature band, energy source), and if met, simulate a coarse evolutionary history (an abstracted timeline, not a creature simulator) that produces a body-level biosphere-richness outcome and a habitability/oxygen-level consequence.
3. **Atmosphere changes as a consequence of that history** — oxygen and other biogenic gases shift the generated atmosphere mix based on whether/how much life emerged, mirroring Shadow Empire's life-alters-atmosphere link. This is still a **one-time generation-time computation** producing a fixed history and a resulting atmosphere state, not an ongoing tick-by-tick weather/climate simulation — deterministic and bounded, per the standing seeded-generation rule.
4. **Presentation** — since this is the player's first impression, the body's generated history (its Planetology/Evolution 'backstory') needs a legible surface, likely a short generated-history readout at body selection/campaign start, not just backing data. Exact UI surface is open — flag for a follow-up design pass once the generation model itself is scoped in TECH detail.

**Architecture: a sibling pass.** Per BL-051's settled pipeline-shape decision this sprint, this is a **body-level sibling pass** invoked outside/before the six-pass tile pipeline (Planetology logically precedes Geology, i.e. tile generation, in Shadow Empire's own ordering) — not a modification to the six-pass core.

**Authority: new doc.** This is a body-level history/chemistry system, a distinct concern from tile-level terrain generation — gets its own authority doc, **docs/generation/PLANETOLOGY.md**, cross-referenced from TILE_GENERATION.md (which it now precedes) and GENERATION_STRATEGY.md (the cross-cutting generation map). Doc creation is this item's own delivery, not scoped here.

**Priority/parking: un-parked, raised to B.** Ben's call: this is no longer a speculative maybe — it's a first-impression pillar for the game, reprioritized accordingly. Still **post-v0.1.0** (a body-history/chemistry system is real scope beyond the prototype's economy-loop arc), but now a real, committed post-prototype item, not a parked one.

**Determinism.** Hard requirement, unchanged — the Planetology/Evolution pass must be a pure deterministic function of the campaign seed, same as every other generation pass (io-standing-rules.md).

**Open for the next design pass (not settled here):** the exact chemistry model's fidelity (how detailed 'basic chemistry' goes), the evolutionary-history abstraction's shape (a fixed set of possible history 'archetypes' vs a richer simulated timeline), and the presentation surface named in point 4.

### R&D pass landed 2026-07-21 (Sprint 1) — chemistry researched, calls owed
**The chemical chain from (A) input solar system → (B) life → (C) civilisation is now modelled end to end** in the authority doc, docs/generation/PLANETOLOGY.md. Ten gated stages (System → Accretion → Air → Engine → Water → Spark → Breath → Green → Legacy → Spend), each a threshold test on already-computed scalars rather than a simulation, each emitting one dated timeline line. Researched across 13 domains with an adversarial fact-check per domain; real quantitative anchors throughout (cosmic shoreline v_esc^4/S normalised to Mars=1.0 reproducing the observed 11-body split; Kopparapu S_eff limits 1.0512/0.3438; radiogenic effective half-life 2.06 Gyr; ozone full-shield at 5–10% PAL not 1%; oil window 60–120 C; ~90% of coal beds in one ~107 Myr window; copper needing 150–350x concentration against iron’s 5–12x).

**The B→C joint — the part Ben specifically asked about — is concrete, not hand-waved.** A biosphere physically manufactures the industrial base: banded iron (>60% of world iron reserves, window OPENING with an Fe-oxidising biosphere and CLOSING at deep-ocean oxidation), petroleum (marine algal, so gated on microbial-not-complex life), coal (land plants + everwet basins + subsidence), bauxite/laterite and supergene copper (both requiring free O2), and soil (requiring biological nitrogen fixation). No life, no coal. Microbes only, and you get colossal iron and real oil but no forests, no soil, and no fire.

**Homeworld rule settled in shape:** constrain the INPUTS (sample the homeworld orbit/mass/water from the sub-region where the identical unmodified chain succeeds), never clamp the gates or the outputs. Variation comes from gate MARGINS, chiefly the iron/coal antagonism — one number (when the deep ocean stopped being ferruginous) trades iron against coal in opposite directions with every gate passed.

**11 open calls are recorded in the doc and are Ben’s, not settled.** The two load-bearing ones: (1) at current scope the feature produces ONE interesting body — Cinder/Selene/Pallas all terminate at stage 1–3 and Kepler is the constrained homeworld, so six of thirteen archetypes and the whole S5–S8 ladder are dead code until world_params::body_count is activated; (2) deposit_scalar (BL-114) ownership must be reconciled before implementation, not discovered at merge. Also flagged: the model is honest that its endowment framing is a game contrivance and that several load-bearing thresholds (BIF oxidant, abiogenesis probability, fire minimum, ozone gate) sit on contested science.

### Landed 2026-07-21/22 — the chain, and the New World wizard
**Shipped.** `src/world/planetology.{hpp,cpp}`: ten gated stages (System, Accretion, Air, Engine,
Water, Spark, Breath, Green, Legacy, Spend) as a sibling pass run before generate_body_tiles, per
BL-051's convention. Each stage is a threshold test on already-computed scalars, not a simulation,
and emits one dated history line; the interesting output is which gate a body died at.

**It derives the body_profile** that used to be four hand-authored literals in hard_coded_world.cpp.
23 of 24 fields reproduce the authored values exactly (Kepler bit-identical, so the homeworld surface
is unchanged). The single divergence is Cinder's geological_activity: authored 'high', derives 'low'
— Mercury is genuinely geologically dead and the authored value was flavour. Costs Cinder some
mountain/rift cluster seeds.

**Two tile-pipeline hooks**, both taking an optional const planetology_state* so a null state
reproduces the pre-BL-167 surface bit-for-bit: a biotic composition mask in Pass 4 (falling back to
composition_abiotic, which mirrors the biotic branch's RNG consumption draw-for-draw so the two stay
stream-aligned), and the per-resource endowment multiply in Pass 6 alongside deposit_scalar.

**Ben's calls.** (1) 'One planet with life is much better for what I'm imagining' — the unreachable
archetype rungs are the intended shape, not a gap; closes the dead-code open call. (2) The one-shot
flow became a per-stage WIZARD: 'I would prefer that the user sees each stage and chooses at each
stage. This helps the user see how the process works and makes it more impressive.' Presented with
charts in the tile-selection idiom.

**The wizard** (app.cpp): ten stages, each with an explainer of the actual chemistry, live charts of
the system as it currently stands, and that stage's decision. Air and Legacy carry NO knob — the
first is a consequence of earlier choices, the second is the payoff — and the UI says so rather than
inventing one. Four new decision points beyond the original six: home_mass, radiogenic,
abiogenesis_ease, coal_climate. radiogenic is deliberately independent of metallicity (U/Th come from
rare r-process events, so a metal-rich system need not be geologically live).

**Charts** are src/ui/charts.{hpp,cpp}, EXTRACTED from the tile-selection deposit graphs (BL-123) so
both surfaces share one implementation rather than imitating each other. Verified pixel-neutral: the
tile golden's diff is byte-identical to the figure measured before the refactor (4.7980%, which is
pre-existing staleness, not this change). Adds tight_ceil (a finer axis ladder than nice_ceil),
threshold_line (a gate drawn on the same axis as the values it judges), and an explicit bar_cap so
wide charts auto-fit while the tile graphs keep their mockup-fixed 34px columns.

**Shared prototype body set.** The four bodies' authored physical facts live once, in planetology.cpp,
reached via prototype_body()/prototype_body_seed(). make_hard_coded_world and the wizard's live
preview_system() walk the same list with the same seeds, so the charts a player decides against
cannot drift from the world actually built.

**Verification: tools/verify/planetology_harness.cpp**, auto-registered as a CTest. R1 determinism,
R2 archetypes + derived profiles, R3 the B->C joint (no life no coal; no aqueous history no clay;
airless bodies keep polar ice), R4 the iron/coal antagonism with both dial ends still passing every
gate, R5 the homeworld corridor across the whole knob space (100/100), R6 WIZARD STABILITY (a
decision at stage N never rewrites the history of a stage before N — what makes Back/Continue safe,
asserted for all seven knobs), R7 every new knob moves its own outcome. Visual check:
scripts/verify/planetology_generation.lua captures all ten wizard stages plus the menu and the
resulting surface. All 22 CTest targets pass.

**The harness caught five real defects before the feature was ever seen:** Selene's tidal term
overflowed to ~3e11 (raw AU fed into an a^-7.5 exponent), Cinder was mis-banded a whole temperature
class by a wet-planet albedo on bare rock, Selene grew clay it cannot have, Pallas reported 0 K by
exiting before instellation was computed, and the iron endowment saturated its clamp so both ends of
the oxygenation dial returned the same number.

**Known dormancy.** The biotic terrain mask has no body to fire on in the shipped set — it only bites
on a world that HAS an atmosphere yet never reached land, and Kepler is the only atmospheric body and
always lives. Built, correct, and exercised by a synthetic small-wet-world case in the harness.

**Still open** (PLANETOLOGY.md § Open calls): deposit_scalar (BL-114) ownership vs the endowment,
resource-list expansion (limestone has the strongest case), spatial ore provinces vs body-level
scalars, survey-gating the report, the report's permanent home, the fire threshold as hard gate vs
soft penalty, and whether the homeworld's joint iron/fuel floor is stated or hidden.

BL-169.design:
**Feasibility question — no build yet.** The world is a seeded, hard-coded Earth-like solar system (make_hard_coded_world; TILE_GENERATION.md prototype body profiles). This item asks how feasible **alternative solar geometry** is — different body counts, orbital arrangements, or non-Earth-like configurations — and what it would cost across the Solar canvas layout (CANVASES.md / SOLAR.md), the zoom ladder, generation, and determinism. Deliverable of this item is a **feasibility note**, not code: what is parameterised vs hard-coded today, what would have to generalise, and whether it feeds a mechanic (Trade/Conflict) or is variety for its own sake. **Parked (F), post-v0.1.0** — the prototype validates the economy loop on the fixed world; solar-geometry variation is out of scope until then. Revisit as a scoping exercise, not a feature, when the prototype is cut. Authority → GENERATION_STRATEGY.md. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

## SETTLED 2026-08-02 — the criterion is answered; it STAYS PARKED, and the note's scope is now defined

The item asks a real question ("does it feed a mechanic, or is it variety for its own sake") and
that question can be answered now without the code survey.

### It does feed Trade — through haul distance

Orbital arrangement determines inter-body convoy distance, and distance is **economically real**:
BL-191's haul-distance pricing already makes a good's price depend on how far it travelled, and
BL-263 has just made that mechanism load-bearing for every outpost market's opening prices.

So alternative geometry is not cosmetic. A compact system and a spread one produce genuinely
different trade economies — different arbitrage margins, different viability thresholds for
off-world extraction. **That is a mechanic, not variety.**

But it is **variety-with-a-mechanic, not a mechanic in itself** — it changes the parameters of
a loop rather than adding one. That is exactly the profile of work that should stay parked
until the loop it parameterises is proven, which is what the prototype cut is for.

**Stays parked (F), post-v0.1.0. Confirmed, not merely inherited.**

### What the feasibility note must contain, so it is finishable

The deliverable is a note, and a note without a scope is how an item stays open forever. It is
done when it answers:

1. **What is parameterised vs hard-coded today** — body count, orbital radii, the Solar canvas's
   layout assumptions, and the zoom ladder's assumption that every body has one parent.
2. **What breaks first at N bodies** — most likely the Solar canvas layout and the minimap, not
   generation.
3. **Whether tile generation generalises** — TILE_GENERATION.md's prototype body profiles are

BL-170.design:
**Idea — design owed.** Surface hydrology today is coarse: a per-body hydrological state and noise-banded oceans (TILE_GENERATION.md six-pass pipeline); there are no rivers and no inland freshwater. This item proposes generating **rivers** across the tile map, most naturally as a downhill trace over the existing height field (the same noise field that bands oceans), from high ground to ocean/basin. Sits with [[BL-167]] (climate) as the hydrology/climate enrichment cluster. Authority → TILE_GENERATION.md when designed. Ben ideas thread 2026-07-10.

### Settled 2026-07-21 (Ben) — supersedes the 2026-07-21 (round 1) tile-flag settle
**A river is an edge, not a tile.** Ben's call: a river borders **exactly two tiles** — it never occupies a tile itself (that would be a lake, a distinct, unrelated feature — not scoped here). Generation is unchanged in spirit (a downhill trace over the height field, high ground → ocean/basin) but the trace now walks the tile **edge graph**: each traced step marks the shared edge between the two tiles it crosses, not the tile itself. Storage: a per-tile bitmask of which of its 6 hex sides border a river reads cheaply from either tile without a separate edge-object store.

**Mechanic: cheaper logistics, not adjacency.** Ben's framing: 'logistics is always point-based — even if it can multiply, it has to cross a tile.' The existing road/logistics traversal cost is per-tile (the `road_level` tier curve, SUPPLY.md). A tile that **borders a river edge** gets a cheaper traversal weight on top of that curve — riverside tiles are cheaper to move goods across, stacking with (not replacing) the road-tier discount, mirroring the structural slot road tiers already occupy. This **replaces** the round-1 framing where a river only granted water-adjacency for farming — the primary mechanic is now logistics, though the water-adjacency read for [[BL-166]]/[[BL-168]]-style farming still holds as a secondary consequence (a tile bordering a river is also water-adjacent).

**Direction is mechanical.** Upstream/downstream is tracked per edge and **changes the traversal cost asymmetrically** — downstream crossing is cheaper than upstream, the same shape as the road tier's directionless-but-tiered discount, just now direction-sensitive. Rendering the direction (open art call, Ben's for now): propose a **shade gradient** — darker blue upstream, lighter/brighter blue downstream — as the simplest reading with no new glyph, consistent with existing terrain-tint rendering; a firmer call belongs to whoever builds the render pass.

**Not a resource.** Still no distinct freshwater good seeded — the mechanic is entirely the logistics discount (+ the water-adjacency side-effect), no new market good.

**Determinism.** Unchanged — the edge trace is still a deterministic function of the seeded height field (standing rule).

**Authority.** TILE_GENERATION.md for the edge-trace generation pass; SUPPLY.md gains the river discount alongside the road-tier table once landed (stacking rule lives there).

Logistics gains river_edge_discount (downstream 0.75x, upstream 0.85x) stacking multiplicatively with the road-tier discount in logistics.cpp A* edge cost. river_generation_harness (new) + a determinism_harness bitmask-identity check both pass; full CTest 37/37 green. BL-172.design:
**Built 2026-07-11 (Ben: 3-tier ladder, ship end-to-end; railroad → [[BL-173]]). Full-mode, main-session-serial** (the pieces are interdependent — the registry struct change ripples to placement + the build front door — so fan-out buys nothing).

**A. Render span/symmetry fix** (`body_surface_canvas.cpp`, the wrap-copy road block). Replace the right/down rectangular offsets + 'both ends roaded, drawn once' scheme with: for each roaded tile, iterate all 6 odd-r hex neighbours (the even_off/odd_off tables the Country-lens border pass already uses); for each neighbour that is roaded, survey-revealed and land, draw a line from this tile's screen centre to the MIDPOINT of the centre-to-neighbour-centre line, styled by THIS tile's tier. Each tile owns its half, so the two halves meet at the shared-edge midpoint (continuous, symmetric) and the survey fog clips cleanly at the boundary. Cylinder-seam wrap handled per neighbour (shift the neighbour screen-x by ±period when the raw column crossed the seam). The 4-cardinal logistics path is a subset of the 6 hex neighbours, so every generated/placed road edge is now drawn.

**B. Tier ladder.** road_level values: 1=Track, 2=Road, 3=Highway. `road_traversal_multiplier` (logistics.cpp) is unchanged — the existing 1/(1+0.5·tier) curve already yields 0.67/0.50/0.40 for the three tiers (diminishing returns). NOTE: roads model cost-discount, not a throughput cap (per-node capacity is out of prototype scope, SUPPLY.md) — 'lower throughput' = lower tier = less discount.

**C. Generation** (`road_generation.cpp`). Rename constants kLocal/kTrunk → kTrack(1)/kRoad(2)/kHighway(3); add kMidScale=2. Edge tier by the two centres' scales: both major (scale≥kMajorScale=3, City/Metropolis) → Highway; at least one Town+ (scale≥2) → Road; else → Track. Cross-nation border links stay Track (lowest). Deterministic (pure over scales/tiles); the astar_cost_cache clear at the end is unchanged.

**D. Economy/registry** (`recipe_registry.{hpp,cpp}`, `economy.lua`). `road_economics` (flat credits + per-resource materials) is unchanged as a struct; the registry now holds a `std::array<road_economics,3>` (Track/Road/Highway) and `road_econ(tier)` returns the tier's cost. Lua `economy.roads` becomes `track/road/highway` sub-tables; the loader reads all three. Defaults (also used by the Lua-free harnesses): Track 25cr/3 steel, Road 45cr/6, Highway 90cr/14.

**E. Placement** (`placement_rules.{hpp,cpp}`, `construction.{hpp,cpp}`). `place_road(w, reg, corp, tile, tier=1)` and `can_place_road(tc, tier=1)`. Upgrade-in-place: valid when non-ocean AND tile.road_level < tier (so you can raise a Track to a Highway but not re-lay the same/lower tier — `already_road` now means 'already at or above this tier'). Cost = the chosen tier's `road_econ(tier)`. Sets road_level=tier, clears astar_cost_cache (unchanged contract). The tier default 1 keeps every existing caller behaviour-identical.

**F. UI plumbing** (`ui_state.hpp`, `app.cpp`, `selection_panel.cpp`). `construction.pending_road_tile` gains a companion `pending_road_tier`; the build front door lists three road affordances (Track/Road/Highway), each with its own cost line + validity (greyed when tile.road_level ≥ tier or unaffordable); app passes the tier to place_road.

**G. Tools stay green.** `road_generation_harness.cpp` R2: assert Track+Road+Highway all present and the ceiling is road_level≤3 (was ≤2). `logistics_harness.cpp` T10: place Track (tier 1), expect the new Track default cost, and add an upgrade-succeeds / same-tier-rejected pair. Visual `roads.lua` extended to show the 3 tiers + the 3 front-door affordances.

**Authority:** SUPPLY.md (tier ladder + multipliers + generation mapping + placement) and GLOSSARY.md (Track/Road/Highway terms); PLANETARY.md/ICONS.md render note (spanning + 3 weights).

**Why:** Ben's steer - a manual workforce percentage is busywork; the interesting decision is the override, not the dial. The solver should land the workforce where marginal wage = marginal margin, then surface that as the default target the player can nudge.

BL-184.design:
**Problem.** `body_surface_canvas.cpp`'s always-on road-edge pass renders three tiers (Track/Road/Highway = `road_level` 1/2/3) purely by line weight and brightness (thin+dim to thick+bright, per SUPPLY.md's ladder). There is no legend anywhere naming which is which, and roads are the only always-on canvas layer with a visual code and no key.

**Why it isn't a trivial drop-in.** Roads are deliberately NOT lens-gated - they render always-on like terrain (Ben's call at BL-147 landing), which is exactly why they were left out of the per-lens legend drawer (BL-164's fold-out legend is keyed to `overlay_mode`, so it only shows when a lens is active). Giving roads a legend means picking a home that doesn't imply 'roads are a lens.'

**Options considered:**
1. **Persistent chip** near the minimap/lens strip, always visible regardless of active lens - three swatches + tier name. Simplest to discover, but adds permanent chrome to an already dense corner (the same crowding concern that deferred this at BL-147/172 landing).
2. **Contextual read** in the Selection panel / hover tooltip when a road tile is hovered or selected - zero permanent chrome cost.
3. **One-time teach** - a dismissible callout the first time the player places or reveals a road, then never again. Teaches once, costs nothing after.

**Determinism/save.** Pure UI/render - no save-format or world-state change.

**Authority.** PLANETARY.md's road-render section already documents the tier ladder's visual encoding; this item adds the legend/teaching mechanism there once landed.

### Settled 2026-07-19 (Ben)
**Option 2 - contextual.** When a road tile is hovered or selected, name the tier ("Highway" etc.) and its traversal discount in the existing per-tile read surface - `draw_tile_selection` (`selection_panel.cpp`, the BL-162-adjacent tile mockup work) for the click path, and the existing hover tooltip in `body_surface_canvas.cpp` for the hover path. No new persistent chrome, no new file. Options 1 and 3 dropped.
BL-184.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.9). Ben ruled the same day: CONTEXTUAL, in Selection/hover -- not a persistent chip by the minimap, and not the lens legend drawer. BL-185.design:
**Current behaviour.** The Planetary canvas's intra-body reach fog (DISCOVERY.md) derives a per-tile `vision` scalar each frame (1 in the permanent layers - own buildings, the corp-centre-to-market corridor - else the moving convoy beam's intensity); the fog wash applies `(1 - vision)` **over the lens fill**, so a fogged tile's analytic read dims with it. The road-edge pass in `body_surface_canvas.cpp` draws independently of that wash, so a road on a `vision ≈ 0` tile still renders at full brightness - identical treatment to a road on a tile the player actively operates.

**Is this actually wrong?** DISCOVERY.md is explicit that 'Survey owns the unrevealed tiles' and the reach fog's semantics are deliberately 'commercial reach, not unknown terrain' (Ben's call at BL-151 landing) - the home planet is the player's own soil, fog means *where your logistics operate*, not *where the land is unmapped*. A road is arguably physical infrastructure like the tile hex itself (visible once surveyed, never re-hidden), not activity knowledge - in which case full-bright-once-surveyed is correct and the DEVLOG deferral was a false alarm.

**The other reading.** The reach fog's whole point is to make the player's own commercial footprint pop (BL-154: 'your trade spine is always lit'). A road you've never trafficked competes visually with the corridors you actively use; dimming untouched roads the same as the lens fill would sharpen that contrast rather than contradict the fog's intent.

**Options considered:**
1. **Leave as-is** - roads are physical terrain, not activity; close this out by adding a line to DISCOVERY.md/PLANETARY.md stating the exclusion is deliberate, so the deferral doesn't resurface as a phantom bug.
2. **Dim roads by `(1 - vision)`** the same alpha multiply the lens fill already receives, reusing the per-tile `vision` value `body_surface_canvas.cpp` already computes - one multiply in the road draw pass, no new state.

**Determinism/save.** `vision` is already frame-derived, non-serialised VIEW state per DISCOVERY.md's stated invariant (never fed back into `world/*`) - either option is a pure render change.

### Settled 2026-07-19 (Ben)
**Option 2 - dim by vision.** Apply the same `(1 - vision)` alpha multiply the lens fill already receives to the road segment's draw colour in the road-edge pass (`body_surface_canvas.cpp`), reusing the existing per-tile `vision` value - no new state. DISCOVERY.md gains a line noting roads participate in the reach-fog wash like the lens fill, closing the physical-vs-activity ambiguity in favour of 'your own footprint outranks infrastructure you don't use.'
BL-185.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.9). The item posed this as a genuinely open question -- 'Is this actually wrong?' -- with a real argument on each side; Ben ruled YES, dim roads with vision. Roads now go through the same `(1 - vision)` wash as the lens fill, via a new `fog_dim()` helper that both call, so the fog is literally one wash rather than two treatments that resemble each other. PER-EDGE COMBINATION IS max(vision of the two tiles), for two recorded reasons: BL-172 makes a span continuous by having each tile draw its half to the shared midpoint, and max is the only cheap combiner under which both halves compute the same value (any other leaves a bright half meeting a dark half mid-span); and reach is a flood outward from where the player operates, so an edge touching a reached tile is inside that reach. Junction centre caps take the brightest edge meeting there, so a cap never renders as a dark blot on the end of a lit span. `fog_dim` preserves alpha where the existing `lerp_colour` forces opaque -- roads are translucent (205/225/238) and would otherwise have changed how they read. Survey masking untouched: unrevealed tiles still skip the road pass entirely. DISCOVERY.md records the rule. NOT VERIFIED: whether 0.5*(1-vision) is the right amount for a thin LINE as opposed to a fill, and whether the max rule leaves a visible one-tile lit fringe at a corridor's rim (it will, by construction -- that is the intended trade-off, but only Ben can say if it looks right).

BL-191.design:
**Ben's ask (2026-07-22):** "Currently markets trade the same essential goods for space travel. Let's also insert C -> D. Before civilisation, resources such as tobacco should be generated, giving essential profit margins for trading based on geopolitical distance."

**The mechanic.** This is the same joint as B -> C on a different axis. B -> C asks what a world can BUILD with; C -> D asks what it is worth CARRYING FROM.

| | Made by | Value comes from |
|---|---|---|
| B -> C | the biosphere | **utility** - coal burns, iron bears load |
| C -> D | the biosphere | **scarcity by geography** - it only grows THERE |

Endemism is the real mechanism, and it is real history: nutmeg (Banda Islands), cinchona (Andes), tobacco (Americas) were worth crossing oceans for not because they were useful like iron but because you could not grow them at home.

**The problem it solves.** Every market previously traded the same industrial goods, so there was no structural reason to trade BETWEEN markets - only local shortage. Endemic goods create trade that exists because of where things are.

**Four goods, one per climate band:** tobacco (temperate/subtropical grassland), spices (tropical wetland/forest), coffee (subtropical forest), furs (subpolar/polar tundra). resource_count 19 -> 23. Safe to insert mid-enum: Lua binds resources by NAME through recipe_registry's lookup table, not by index, and no serialiser exists yet.

**Generation.** A new stage in run_planetology, gated on `life_stage >= land` - so the C -> D stage sits downstream of B -> C and a world with no forests has no cash crops either. Each good rolls whether this biosphere produced it at all (~60-70% each, mean 2.65 of 4 per world), then gets a latitude band (fixed per good) AND a longitude sector + width (rolled). The SECTOR is what makes it endemic rather than merely climatic: two worlds can both have temperate grassland and only one grow tobacco.

**Placement.** In tile_generation Pass 6, guarded by the planetology state. Unlike the BL-167 endowment - which SCALES an existing deposit - this ADDS one, because an endemic good has no base distribution to scale. A tile qualifies on band AND (wrapped) sector AND a composition the crop grows on; density falls off toward the sector edge so a region has a centre worth holding rather than a hard border.

**Pricing needed NO change to the clearing engine.** `market_component::base_price` is already per-market and authored at world creation, so an endemic good is simply cheap at its origin and dear far from it; supply/demand then push around that base as for any resource. `base_price = 1.5 x (1 + 7.0 x normalised_distance_to_nearest_source)`.

**Measured on a generated world:** tobacco 2.45 -> 8.19 (x3.34), spices 3.72 -> 7.56 (x2.03), coffee 1.84 -> 8.59 (**x4.67**). At the far end these beat steel (8.0). **The scarcest good commands the widest margin, and that is emergent rather than authored** - coffee had 30 source tiles against tobacco's 179, so it is further from more markets. Nobody tuned that.

**Distance is PHYSICAL for now.** Ben's call: "Let's leave it as just distance now. The word geopolitical will carry a weight when we add diplomacy and basic AI behaviour." The multiplier gains a political term later rather than being replaced.

**Verification:** planetology_harness R9 (a land biosphere evolves them; sterile/airless/core-fragment bodies evolve none; every good occurs on SOME world but none on EVERY world, so scarcity is real; each is confined to one band and one sector) and R10 (against a fully built world: the trade margin exists, and an endemic good covers only a small share of the land).

**Surfaced** in the New World wizard's Inheritance round as its own chart plus a line per good naming the band and region it grows in - the band and region ARE the value, so they are stated rather than left implicit.

**Open / deferred:** no dedicated extraction building yet (they generate as tile deposits and are extracted by the existing path); the goods are Kepler-only because markets are Kepler-only in the prototype - the same code gives the large off-world premium once markets exist elsewhere, which is the Era-0-trade-pays-for-Era-1 hook.
