BL-269.design: FILED 2026-08-02 from planetary-pan-perf R4 (BL-268's whole-grid residual). Design-owed: two candidate directions, not yet chosen — (a) zoom-LOD: below a zoom threshold draw tiles as flat quads or single AddRectFilled cells (no per-hex 6-vertex polys, no relief/road/marker detail that is sub-pixel at that scale anyway); (b) terrain draw cache: render the static layers (terrain fill + relief + lens tint) into an SDL texture once per (body, lens, survey-state) key and blit it, re-rendering only when one of those changes — dynamic chrome (markers, borders, beams, hover) stays immediate-mode on top. (b) is the bigger win and the bigger change (a texture target enters the renderer path); (a) is an afternoon. Measure first at the actual min zoom: BL-249's instrument + pan_perf z0.9 phase are the harness. NOT a backend swap — BL-267's verdict stands.
BL-269.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09. Direction (a), zoom-LOD, chosen by Ben after the measurement below; direction (b), the terrain draw cache, was NOT built -- (a) delivered enough that a texture render target could not be justified yet. WHY IT WAS PICKED UP NOW: Ben reported panning 'lags, but that manifests as occasional sharp jumps' and proposed a ~200ms delay before panning engages. Measuring first overturned the diagnosis. pan_perf on Kepler (15,120 tiles) showed the STATIC and PANNING phases at the same zoom are identical -- 157,084 vs 158,407 vertices, 14.25 vs 14.40 ms submit -- so panning costs nothing. The cost is the whole-grid ZOOM: 157k vertices against 6,172 one notch in, a 25x cliff, with submit alone (14.25 ms) blowing the 8 ms frame budget before the GPU does anything. The jumps are therefore a rendering symptom, not an input one: the pan is `pan += io.MouseDelta`, which is 1:1 and correct, so a frame taking 3x as long applies 3x the accumulated delta at once -- the right destination by a jumpy route. A delay would have ADDED latency to a 1:1 drag (world lags the cursor, then snaps) without touching frame cost. THE FIX: `AddConvexPolyFilled(verts, 6, ...)` costs ~10 vertices per tile once the AA fringe is counted; `AddRectFilled` costs 4 and emits no fringe. Below a threshold the canvas draws the terrain fill as a rect. THRESHOLD IS DERIVED, NOT PICKED: a hexagon differs from its inscribed rect by `draw_r * (1 - sqrt(3)/2)` = `draw_r * 0.134`, which falls under one pixel at draw_r < 7.46, so the bound is 7 px (corner cut 0.94 px there, and the per-tile landform icons at 0.42*draw_r are already unreadable). A first attempt used 5 px and did not fire at all -- at a 1080-tall window the whole-grid view sits at draw_r ~5.1-5.7 -- which is the argument for deriving the bound from geometry rather than eyeballing a constant that works at one window size. ONE REAL DEFECT FOUND BY LOOKING: the first working version sized the rect from the hex RADIUS and the terrain rendered as horizontal stripes. Rows step by 1.5*hex_size while a hex is 2*hex_size tall, so consecutive rows overlap; a radius-sized rect is shorter than the row pitch and leaves gaps. Sized to the grid step (col_step x row_step) the rects brick-lay and tile the plane exactly, because odd rows are offset half a column. Caught by capturing the canvas and looking at it, not by any assertion. MEASURED, whole-grid view: vertices 157,084 -> 63,004 (-60%), submit 14.25 ms -> 4.25 ms (-70%). Zoomed-in phases are byte-identical in vertex count (6,172 and 23,620), confirming the LOD does not fire where detail is readable. UNAFFECTED: terrain colour, relief shading, the survey mask and the fog wash are colour rather than geometry, so the analytic read the whole-grid view exists for is unchanged. The visible difference is that the far-zoom grid texture is brick-laid rather than hex-dotted. NOT DONE: BL-267's verdict stands, this is not a backend swap; and no attempt was made on `build_ms` (~9 ms), which is ImGui draw-list construction and the next thing to look at if the whole-grid view is still short of budget on low-spec hardware.
BL-269.summary: The residual BL-268 (canvas cull + cache) deliberately did not chase: with the whole 180x84 grid visible, all 15,120 hexes are genuinely on-screen and ImGui emits ~155k vertices every frame — 12.1 ms work/frame in Release (over the 8 ms audit target; fine against 16.7). Per-tile culling cannot help when everything is visible; the fix is emitting less: coarser geometry at low zoom (hexes to quads/points below a zoom threshold) or caching the static terrain layer to a texture redrawn only on lens/fog/built change. Filed per planetary-pan-perf R4 rather than stretching BL-268. Priority B: the case is the min-zoom overview, where 12 ms still holds 60 fps; it misses only the stricter 8 ms average target.

BL-270.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-02 (Ben, via the elicitation form in the pan-perf session).

## Ben's four settlements (verbatim answers)

1. **Scope: 'Every control including chrome.'** Not just the 8 gameplay verbs, not just verbs + reading controls — literally every press: canvas clicks (select / navigate / place), the keyboard binding table (pan/zoom/lens/speed/descend/ascend, app.cpp's canvas_command table), the nav rail, ledger tabs and sub-views, the lens strip, cross-cutting selectors (body/market/resource combos), time controls, the system menu, the construction panel flow, the Selection band affordances, the comms dock, and the New World wizard's controls.
2. **Entry fields: preconditions + typed arguments** on top of the fixed A/B pair (expected_output, reason_to_select). **Deliberately excluded** (offered, not selected): cost/spend and backlog provenance — the dictionary states what a press does and why you'd press it, not what it costs (that is world-state the blackboard reports) nor which item demanded it (that is UX_QUESTIONS' axis).
3. **Store home: docs/ai/** — 'since the consumer is the AI player'. ACTIONS.json canonical + ACTIONS.md generated mirror (sibling conventions: backlog.json/BACKLOG.md, user_stories.json/USER_STORIES.md), renderer tools/session/render_actions.js modelled on render_needs_review.js.
4. **Consumer: both, in sequence.** 'Dictionary now, generation and play consume it in sequence' — word-driven procedural generation (the New World wizard via words) consumes it first, word-driven gameplay after. Ben's milestone note: 'To consider what the difficulty level will be, we need this item. That is not really one item, it's the whole process of gameplay/development.' The dictionary is the substrate; the milestone is a process, not an item (NR-034 asks where it slots in ROADMAP).

## Entry shape

Per entry: `id` (stable slug), `surface` (where the control lives, human terms), `press` (what the player physically does — click/key/drag), `args` (typed arguments, named and typed as the code takes them — e.g. build: {type: building_type, tile: entity, target: resource_type}), `preconditions` (when the press is valid — for the 8 corp verbs these MUST mirror corp_command_result's rejection semantics exactly: no_corp/not_owner/invalid/placement/funds/state), `expected_output` (A — what observably happens, stated against world/ui state, honest about durative effects like pay-as-you-build), `reason_to_select` (B — why a player or AI would choose this press over alternatives; design intent in plain words).

## Why the seams make this cheap to keep honest

The 8 gameplay verbs already have a single validated entry point (apply_corp_command, 'the contract an out-of-process policy (stage C/D) would return' — corp_command.hpp's own words) with enumerated rejections; expected_output and preconditions for those entries are TRANSCRIBED from code, not invented. The UI chrome entries are authored prose, sourced from the authority docs (CANVASES/LENSES/LAYOUT/SELECTION/STARTUP) — where a doc and the dictionary disagree, that IS the finding.

## Relationship to the siblings

Third axis, companion not replacement: user_stories.json (intent — what the player is trying to do), UX_QUESTIONS.json/BL-260 (information — what question a readout answers), ACTIONS.json (action — what a press does and why). BL-260 stays docs-only per its own settlement; ACTIONS differs in kind because its consumer is a MACHINE player as well as the designer, which is why args and preconditions are typed rather than prose-only.

## Not in scope

- The text-play harness itself (prompt loop: blackboard + dictionary -> LLM -> corp_command). That is the next item in the milestone sequence, filed when the dictionary exists to feed it.
- Word-driven generation (the wizard via words) — consumes the dictionary later; not built here.
- Any in-game rendering of dictionary text (BL-260's NR-018 lesson stands: development documentation does not leak into the UI).
- Audit tooling beyond the mirror renderer's parse (the docs are the audit — Ben's standing position; the machine consumer will find gaps by failing to act, loudly).
BL-270.resolution: LANDED 2026-08-02, same session as filing and promotion. 114 entries across the five families (11 gameplay / 24 canvas / 15 lens / 36 ledger / 28 chrome) in docs/ai/ACTIONS.{json,md}, authored by five parallel family agents and merged with per-fragment validation; render_actions.js generates the mirror and doubles as the shape check. action-dictionary R1-R4 all met — the gameplay family is transcribed from corp_command.hpp (typed args + rejection semantics), and the sweep caught two doc-truth defects in passing: LENSES.md's stale supply-routes unreachability note (fixed) and the undocumented seventh rung of the Esc precedence ladder (transcribed in chrome.esc). AI_OPPONENT.md § 6a and CLAUDE.md § Documents carry the pointers. The next milestone items (the text-play harness; word-driven generation) now have their substrate.
BL-270.summary: Ben, 2026-08-02, filed SSS per his instruction ('it blocks the next most important milestone, which is a word-based procedural generation and later gameplay'): a complete dictionary giving every button press A) expected output and B) reason to select, so an LLM plays via words — the model that will eventually run on-machine, and first a cloud Sonnet/Opus experiment. Scope settled by elicitation same day: EVERY control including chrome; entries carry typed arguments + preconditions beyond the A/B pair; store lives in docs/ai/ (the consumer is the AI player); the consumer sequence is BOTH — dictionary now, word-driven generation then word-driven gameplay consume it in order. This is the third catalogue axis: user_stories.json = intent, UX_QUESTIONS (BL-260) = information surfaces, ACTIONS = the action axis. The write channel already speaks this shape (corp_command.hpp: 8 verbs, 'exactly the player's action surface', typed rejections); BL-206's blackboard export is the read channel; the dictionary is the missing middle.

BL-271.design:
## Settled at filing (2026-08-02 brainstorm)

- **Year tick, own loop.** The economy tick is a day; this needs a year (or campaign-season) tick with its own loop - a NEW loop, not a reuse of the economy tick. Seasonality (campaigning season vs winter / mare-clausum closure) is in from the start because it is half of pre-modern strategy, and it is cheap at this granularity (a season flag on the tick; doctrine and supply modifiers keyed to it).
- **The rupture transforms become recurring systems.** resolve_historical_ruptures' collapse/war/revolution logic is the seed: what fired once as a checkpoint fires each year as an evaluated decision by a nation actor. The checkpoint mechanism (BL-217) stays for one-shot branch points; the sim adds the continuous layer on top.
- **The record-burning rule carries over.** Wars in the sim erase and lacuna-ise the loser's record exactly as BL-218 landed it - 2000 years of that produces worlds whose written history is itself an artifact of who won, which is the philosophical-development payload.
- **Non-hegemony becomes emergent, not asserted.** Some seeds WILL produce a Rome; BL-224's invariant becomes a tuning target read off BL-275's sweep distributions (what parameter regions keep worlds multipolar), not a construction guarantee. The sweep is also the answer to 'what does an averted rupture need to look like' (BL-223).

## Open questions (for the design conversation, not blockers)

1. Determinism/runtime budget: 2000 ticks x ~40 nations x seed spread - integer arithmetic throughout per the standing rule, but what is the wall-clock budget per world? (Working target: a full 0-2000 CE run well under a second, so BL-275 can do hundreds.)
2. What state persists into the 1960 campaign when the sim replaces the pre-computed Stages 3-4 - the full province history, or the same summary the settlement pass produces today? (Cheapest honest answer: the sim RUNS at generation time and writes the same outputs BL-218 writes, plus a richer history log for BL-208's store.)
3. Does the player ever get a seat in the sandbox (crude feel-testing) or is it bot-only? Ben has not answered this; default is bot-only until he does.

## Naming constraint (Ben, 2026-08-03)

This item is filed off a real-history analogy ("use Rome as a sandbox"). Under the standing
rule added the same day (io-standing-rules § Terms & docs; GENERATION_STRATEGY § Real history
in, invented names out), that analogy is a **mechanism** reference only.

What this item takes from Rome: campaign-season structure, supply radii, how a frontier stalls,
how fast a hegemony forms, what makes a littoral power. What it must never take: a proper noun.
Every nation, province, city and commander the sim produces is named from the seeded sci-fi /
fantasy template banks, and the phoneme tables must not read as recognisably Latin — a name a
player can place as "the Roman one" has failed however good the mechanism under it.

Io's existing rule that Rome is *calibration reference, not content* already said this for the
mil-sim; it now applies to the whole Era −1 arc.

## Ruling (Ben, 2026-08-07): elimination and release are design intent

The first sweep (BL-275) found polity elimination and population collapse unreachable across 12 seeds - the no-elimination finding, filed in-session under pre-rebase id BL-308 and retired as a standalone item by this ruling. Its target stands here instead: **polity elimination must be possible, and so must release of subject nations** - death and breakaway are both required outcomes of the sim, not tuning accidents. The physical-constraint half is BL-316's (era -1 logistics) burden-of-breadth slice; the scorer half is the shared-currency redesign in the 2026-08-07 working tree (re-file if it stalls). Release of subject nations is NEW scope: the sim currently has no subject or breakaway mechanism at all.
BL-271.summary: Filed 2026-08-02 from the Ben brainstorm ('use Rome as a sandbox'). The settlement pass (BL-218) already simulates settlement -> industrialisation -> war ONCE, at generation time, then freezes the result. This item promotes it to a running simulation: a YEAR-TICK loop over provinces and nations from 0 CE to the campaign epoch, in which wars, collapses and revolutions recur rather than firing once as checkpoints. PURPOSE IS WRITTEN DOWN AND BOUNDED: this is the proving ground for the nation AI (BL-054's parked runtime half, the BL-155/156 diplomacy/war stubs) and the mil-sim (BL-272), and the instrument for tuning the worlds' 'philosophical development' against a seed spread (BL-275) - it lives behind a harness flag / tools target, never in the shipped campaign path, and it dies into (or is absorbed by) the 1960 era when those systems graduate. TRANSFER CONTRACT stated up front: what transfers to the main era is the ARCHITECTURE (decision loop, spatial reasoning, war/peace evaluation, the combat engine itself), never the tuning constants. Rome is the CALIBRATION REFERENCE, not the content - sea:river:land cost ratios, campaign-season structure (mare-clausum-style closure), army supply radii, plausible hegemony formation speed - while the world itself stays Kepler's own generated antiquity, seed-varied so the AI cannot overfit one map. This item also partially absorbs BL-223's design question: simulating a thousand near-ruptures is how the averted one gets designed against evidence rather than lore.

BL-272.design:
## Settled at filing (2026-08-02 brainstorm)

**'Real tactics' means doctrine parameters, never battlefields.** This is the load-bearing constraint everything else prices off. 2000 years x ~40 nations x a seed spread is millions of engagements; if a battle is a tactical simulation, the sweep is dead on arrival. The workable shape:

- An **army is a stack of typed units** (unit_component grows a type; a stack is a vector of (type, count) pairs).
- A **battle is ONE deterministic evaluation**: unit-type matchup matrix x formation doctrine x BL-233's terrain scalars (terrain_defence / terrain_attrition / terrain_resistance, landed 2026-07-31 - and this is finally their intended consumer, per HISTORY.md's BL-224 note) x supply state x season.
- **Tactics are data, not manoeuvres**: a doctrine row reads like 'phalanx - devastating frontal, brittle flank, useless in mountain'. Rock-paper-scissors with historical teeth: a doctrine is a set of modifiers against the matchup matrix and the terrain scalars, nothing more.
- **Integer arithmetic with explicit tie-breaks** throughout - battle outcomes are gate-path decisions (they move borders), so the float ban applies.

**Engine parity contract:** the same resolve function serves the Era -1 sim and the 1960+ era; only the roster table (BL-274) and the doctrine table differ. No sandbox-only combat rules - anything the sandbox needs, the main era gets.

## Open questions

1. Matchup matrix size: per unit-type pair, or per class pair (infantry / cavalry / ranged / siege / naval) with type-level modifiers? (Lean: class pair + modifiers - the matrix stays readable and rosters stay cheap to extend.)
2. Naval combat: same engine with a sea 'terrain', or deferred? (Sea-cheap logistics makes navies strategically decisive before they are tactically interesting - lean: strategic-only naval presence first, engine extension later.)
3. Sieges/attrition vs field battles: the ancient norm is that attrition and supply kill more than battle does. Does the first cut model sieges as a doctrine ('assault' vs 'invest') or as a separate resolution path?
BL-272.resolution: Landed 2026-08-02 as Sprint 5's foundation wave. `resolve_battle` in src/world/combat.{hpp,cpp}: two army stacks (vector of {type_id, unit_class, count, type_power_mod}) + two doctrine_row values + terrain + season + supply -> battle_outcome (result, power tallies, integer per-mille losses, decisiveness). Lean taken on all three open questions: class-pair matchup matrix with per-type modifiers; naval entries contribute zero tactical power (strategic-only); sieges are a doctrine (siege_stance::assault/invest), not a separate resolution path. unit_component gained a type field (opaque roster index; BL-274 owns interpreting it). tools/verify/combat_harness.cpp 15/15 PASS (determinism, terrain flipping an outcome, tie-break, bounded losses, doctrine-drives-same-function, naval exclusion). Full CTest suite 41/41 green after merge to main.
BL-272.summary: OVERTURNED DECISION, recorded here at Ben's instruction rather than parked in NEEDS_REVIEW (Ben, 2026-08-02): since BL-221 the rule has been that simulated-history wars resolve as ABSTRACT scalar comparisons (record_tribal_conflict, the rupture war branch - zeal/dominion/terrain numbers, no units). Ben overturns the abstract half: simulated history uses REAL ancient units and real military tactics, as typed unit types that later exist in the main era. The 'drives, does not narrate' half SURVIVES untouched - battles still move borders, abundance and the record. The strongest argument for the overturn: unit_component in the 1960 game is a stub (count=50, nothing else), so the sandbox does not borrow the main era's military model - it DEFINES it. One combat engine, era-keyed rosters (BL-274), and the 1960 game inherits a mil-sim with two thousand years of regression tests behind it.

BL-273.design:
## Settled at filing (2026-08-02 brainstorm)

- **Logistic growth per province**, integer fixed-point, carrying capacity derived from the province's farm endowment (the world-relative farm_q BL-218 already computes) - the ground feeds who it can feed. Growth modulated by war (drawdown at battles fought on or by the province) and by rare plague events (a checkpoint-class draw reusing BL-217's mechanism - eligibility-filtered, recorded, never a weight).
- **Manpower is the army budget**: a nation's recruitable stock is a fraction of its provinces' population, and units raised deplete it. This closes the loop that makes 2000-year wars self-limiting - the reason ancient hegemonies stall is manpower exhaustion, and the sim should reproduce that from the model rather than from a cap.
- **Feeds the existing surfaces on graduation**: at the 1960 handoff the province populations seed the population-centre scales (today drawn from a weighted distribution), so the demography the sim earned replaces a die roll - the same pattern as every other BL-210-era rewrite.

## Open questions

1. Granularity: population per province only, or with an urban/rural split? (Lean: province total first; the split is a refinement the 1960 agglomeration model can add.)
2. Plague as global events (Antonine-plague-shaped, hitting connected provinces harder - trade connectivity as the vector, which makes the sea lanes double-edged) or as local draws? The connectivity version is more interesting and reads straight off the logistics graph.
3. Does carrying capacity move when industrialisation arrives? Almost certainly yes - Stage 4's fossil-fuel escape from the organic economy IS a carrying-capacity jump - but the magnitude wants tuning against BL-275's sweep.
BL-273.resolution: Landed 2026-08-02 as Sprint 5's foundation wave. province gains population (int64_t), last_demography_year, manpower_stock; province_carrying_capacity(farm_q) is linear off the existing endowment field; advance_province_demography does integer fixed-point logistic growth + war drawdown; manpower_ceiling/replenish_manpower/raise_manpower give the bounded, self-limiting army budget; resolve_plague_event draws through resolve_checkpoint's eligibility mechanism. Leans taken on the open questions: province-total population (no urban/rural split); plague connectivity via grid (Chebyshev) proximity rather than the full logistics/trade graph, since that graph isn't reachable at this generation stage (noted in POPULATION.md); carrying-capacity response to industrialisation deferred, as scoped. tools/verify/demography_harness.cpp 20/20 PASS. settlement_harness re-verified clean against the extended province struct (21/21). Full CTest suite 41/41 green after merge to main.
BL-273.summary: Armies are population, and the Era -1 sim (BL-271) is unanchored without a manpower model: population centres currently carry a static scale and no growth, so 2000 years of army sizes would float free of anything. This item gives each PROVINCE (the BL-218 unit) a population that grows and is drawn down - the deferred POPULATION.md design finding its first honest consumer, at the coarse granularity the year-tick needs rather than the full agglomeration model the 1960 game eventually wants.

BL-275.design:
## Settled at filing (2026-08-02 brainstorm)

- **Deterministic per seed, comparable across seeds**: same discipline as every harness - a sweep row is replayable from its seed alone.
- **Report, do not gate (at first)**: the sweep's first job is to SHOW Ben the distributions (the BL-219-sweep lesson: Ben asked to see failure cases). Assertions (e.g. 'hegemony rate stays under X%') come after he has seen the raw spread and said what he wants, not before.
- **Named metrics for the first cut**: per-seed final nation count; hegemony events (any nation crossing a territory-share threshold, with the year); wars per century and their average territorial transfer; lacunae per world (how much written history survived); ideology distribution at epoch; first/median/last industrialisation years; population at epoch vs peak.
- **Closes BL-210**: with this landed, the umbrella's last scope item (batch-sweep extension) is met and BL-210 closes after TILE_GENERATION.md's propagation share.

## Open questions

1. Sweep size vs runtime: hangs entirely on BL-271's per-world budget (its open question 1). 100 seeds at under a second each is the working target.
2. Output surface: printed table only, or a JSON the (future) generation ledger / wizard could read? (Lean: JSON + printed summary - the marginal cost is trivial, and the wizard's formed-vs-left chart shows there is appetite for generation evidence in the UI.)
BL-275.resolution: Landed 2026-08-05 ('The history sweep, and the answer it gives is no') as tools/verify/history_sweep.cpp - reports, does not gate; JSON + printed summary per the filed lean. Runtime target missed and said so (0.95-10 s per world, scaling with province count). First spread: hegemony 0/12, elimination 0/12 - the no-elimination finding, retired 2026-08-07 by Ben's ruling with its target recorded on BL-271. Requirements group history-sweep, all rows complete. Status flipped 2026-08-07 during the NR-079 rebase repair: the landing predates the rebase, which dropped the status change.
BL-275.summary: BL-210's one remaining scope item is the batch-sweep extension, and this gives it its real payload: sweep N seeds of earth-like generation through the full 0-2000 CE sim (BL-271) and report DISTRIBUTIONS - hegemony formation rate, war frequency and lethality, ideology mix at epoch, industrialisation onset spread, record-loss (lacunae) rates, population trajectories. Ben, 2026-08-02: 'Once generation produces a spread of earth-like planets, we can refine the crucial philosophical development of our worlds by getting tons of examples which go from 0 CE to 2000 CE.' The sweep is HOW the campaign premise's philosophical claims stop being assertions: BL-224's non-hegemony becomes a measured rate to tune toward, and BL-223's averted rupture gets designed against a thousand simulated near-ruptures instead of lore. Ben has explicitly welcomed hard failure cases ('if a problem becomes very hard to solve, I will be fascinated') - so the sweep reports the ugly distributions honestly rather than tuning them away before he sees them.

BL-276.design:
## Settled at filing (Ben, 2026-08-03 - hybrid, ~90%)

Two levers, per the sweep session's NR-041 options, landed together:

- **Mechanism (consequence, not dice)**: a rift-basin extension to run_continents. Where the boundary classifier finds a DIVERGENT pair of two CONTINENTAL plates, the boundary corridor founders: a strong negative height bias (distance-falloff from the boundary tiles) is stamped into height_bias, so Pass 2's percentile threshold floods it into an inland sea shaped by plate structure. Total ocean stays at water_fraction (the threshold is a percentile), so the basin RELOCATES ocean rather than adding it. Emits one biography line (chain_stage::engine) - the rift that became a sea is readable history. Worlds whose plate draw yields no continental divergent pair get no basin: those are the deliberately-hard ~10%.
- **Backstop gate (selection, reject-and-reroll)**: in hard_coded_world's Kepler wiring, an acceptance loop over the tile seed (attempt-folded XOR, attempt 0 = today's seed) regenerates into a scratch world until SOME enclosed sea >= 30 tiles exists (cap 6 attempts; on exhaustion keep attempt 0 honestly - no clamp, per the resolve_preferences idiom). This is the 'never impossible to try' floor: nearly every world has at least a small enclosed sea, even when the full Mediterranean arena is absent.

**Target numbers** (mediterranean_sweep is the measure): enclosed sea >= 300 tiles in ~88-92% of seeds; enclosed sea >= 30 tiles in ~100%. Do NOT overtune the basin toward 100% at 300 tiles - the hard-Rome tail is wanted.

**Determinism**: the basin pass draws no shared-stream RNG (distance field only; its history line uses the existing per-pair local rng shape), so it cannot perturb plate seeding or downstream passes beyond the intended bias. The gate is a pure function of (campaign seed).
BL-276.resolution: Landed 2026-08-03. Rift-basin mechanism (interior-segment corridor, adaptive width, rift-shoulder rim) + intracratonic sag fallback in run_continents; two-bar acceptance gate (arena >=300 x3 attempts, floor >=30 x6) on Kepler's tile seed in hard_coded_world. Measured over 500 seeds: floor 100%, arena 89.6% (target ~90%; the tail is the wanted hard-Rome set). mediterranean_sweep harness (new, asserted) + continents_harness, world_determinism, determinism_harness, world_audit all PASS. Docs: CONTINENTS.md section, TILE_GENERATION.md deferred note updated.
BL-276.summary: Ben (2026-08-03): a near-Mediterranean structure - an inland sea enclosed by land - should be almost inevitable (~90% of seeds), while the remaining worlds where forming 'something like Rome' is HARD stay interesting; it must never be impossible to try. Measured baseline (tools/verify/mediterranean_sweep.cpp, 500 seeds): an enclosed sea >=300 tiles exists in only 44% of seeds today.

BL-278.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-03 (Ben's steer + the § 10 research sweep).

## Why MCP and not something bespoke

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol over stdio or HTTP: a SERVER exposes
`tools` (callable functions with typed args), `resources` (fetchable read-only data) and
`prompts` (reusable templates); a CLIENT is whatever agent runtime is driving. The field
converged on it independently — Vox Deorum, civ6-mcp, civStation and CivBench all wrap their
game as an MCP server over a fixed verb list. Adopting it costs no originality and buys every
existing client (Claude Code/Desktop, Gemini/Codex CLIs, Ollama-backed local loops, bespoke
harnesses) for free.

## The mapping — near-mechanical, because BL-206 and BL-270 already did the hard parts

| MCP primitive | Io asset |
|---|---|
| `tools` | `corp_command.hpp`'s verbs — already typed, already validated, rejections already enumerated in `corp_command_result` |
| `resources` | `--export-blackboard` JSONL (BL-206) — visibility-honest, deterministic ordering, schema-versioned |
| `prompts` | `reason_to_select` from `ACTIONS.json` (BL-270) — the design-intent prior |
| lookup tool | `actions_query.js` over `ACTIONS_INDEX.json` — hold the index, fetch entries on demand |

## Design calls settled by the research (§ 10c.5)

- **Push state, do not make the model pull it.** CivBench's "sensorium effect" — agents miss
  information they never think to query — is the dominant failure of a purely pull-shaped tool
  surface. The server must lead each turn with the blackboard slice rather than waiting to be
  asked for it. This is the single cheapest quality win available and it is an interface
  decision, not a model decision.
- **Mask to legal primitives.** Only `corp_command` verbs are exposed as tools; the validation
  path is the player's. Fairness is then a property of the seam, not of tuning — and a rejected
  command is a typed, loggable event rather than a silent no-op.
- **Never ask the model to carry world state across turns.** The observation-belief research
  (§ 10c.4, measured on exactly the open-weight class Io targets) shows belief accuracy degrading
  with multi-hop reasoning and drifting from coherence over long interactions. Hand it the state
  every turn.
- **Coarse cadence.** The model chooses strategy occasionally, not per-tick; the BL-202/203
  utility core executes tactically underneath. Unchanged from § 2C.

## Scope

In: the server process, the tool/resource/prompt surface over the three legs, the push-shaped
turn packet, a smoke path proving an attached client can read state and land a legal command.

Out: the trace/corpus format and the fine-tuning pipeline (BL-279); any in-process API call
(NR-039 settled that this never ships inside the exe); any change to `corp_command`'s verb set
— if a verb is missing, that is its own item.

## Determinism

Unaffected. The model is out-of-process, commands still apply at the tick boundary through
player-grade validation, and NR-039's proposed determinism carve-out stays reverted.
BL-278.summary: Ben, 2026-08-03, on reading the public-field research (AI_OPPONENT.md § 10): "We can use MCP." The wrapper NR-040 was groping for. Io already has all three legs of the word interface — BL-206's blackboard export (read), BL-270's action dictionary (meaning), corp_command (write); MCP is the standard socket that turns them into something any agent runtime drives. Ships no HTTP client and no API key inside ProjectIo.exe — the server is a separate local process, and with nothing attached the game is byte-identical to today. Model-agnostic by construction, which is the whole point: the same server serves a cloud frontier model generating traces (BL-279) and the small local model those traces produce. VERSION GOAL v0.1.1 (Ben, 2026-08-03, NR-044): the server touches no simulation code, and its whole value is enabling a first real text-driven play attempt — landing it early is the "try it cheaply before designing more" lesson NR-040 already taught once. BL-279 (corpus) stays v0.2.0; it cannot start until traces exist.

BL-281.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-03 (Ben, NR-020 option 2).

**The change.** The History ledger drops to two views — **Story** and **Chain** — which share a
single honest premise: how this world came to be. The Tiles view is removed, not renamed.

**Why retirement beats renaming.** Renaming to 'Body' or 'Buildings & Market' would fix the
label and keep the real defect: a current-state readout living inside a ledger about the past.
The ledger's premise is what makes its two remaining views legible together; a third view about
now weakens it. Both orphaned sections already have homes — buildings are on the canvas and in
the Selection element, market data is in the market surfaces.

**What comes down with it.**

- The `history_tiles` fold surface — this view's table is currently the *example* case in
  `scripts/verify/drill_through_fold.lua`, so that check needs a new subject or a narrower
  scope. Pick a surviving fold surface rather than deleting the assertion.
- Any nav-rail / tab wiring for the third sub-view, per the toggle rule (re-clicking the active
  tab closes the ledger; with two tabs that behaviour must still hold).

**Check before landing.** Confirm nothing else reads the removed builder — the per-entity
content builders are shared with the Tile Ledger and the hover card (SELECTION.md), so the

BL-281.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.9). BL-282.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-03 (Ben, NR-030 option 2).

**The change.** In `credit_arrived_convoys`, the first-establishment branch
(`rit == w.trade_routes.end()`) pushes **two** `world_history_entry` records instead of one —
one tagged `src_body`, one tagged `dest_body` — carrying the same narration naming both
endpoints. A body-scoped filter then finds the route from either side.

**Why this over widening the struct.** Adding a `body_b` field would change a struct four other
call sites depend on, for one topic's need, and would leave every other topic carrying a field
it never sets. Two tagged entries keep the struct's one-body invariant intact and keep every
existing reader correct without modification.

**The cost, stated honestly.** Route establishment doubles in log volume. That is bounded by
the body-pair count rather than by convoy traffic — a route is logged once, not per delivery —
so the absolute growth is small. Duplicated narration for a single event is the real price; a
reader rendering the log chronologically will see the same sentence twice with different body
tags. Mitigation if that reads badly: keep the narration identical and let a renderer
de-duplicate on (tick, event) when it is not filtering by body.

**Verification.** `history_log_harness.cpp` gains an assertion that a newly established route
yields exactly two entries, that their body tags are the two distinct endpoints, and that
filtering by either endpoint returns the route. The determinism check must still pass — entry
order within the tick has to be stable (src before dest, not iteration-order dependent).
BL-282.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.10). credit_arrived_convoys's first-establishment branch now pushes TWO world_history_entry records, one tagged src_body and one tagged dest_body, carrying the same narration -- so a body-scoped filter finds the route from either side. Order is fixed SOURCE THEN DESTINATION rather than iteration-dependent, so replays stay byte-identical. The struct is untouched, which was the point: NR-030 option 2 chose this over adding a `body_b` field precisely because that would change a struct four other call sites depend on, for one topic's need, and leave every other topic carrying a field it never sets. COST MEASURED, not assumed. From data_creep_harness on a real generated world (1500 ticks, 1500 seeded convoys, 1496 credited): world.trade_routes reaches 18 keys and LAST GROWS AT TICK 36. So trade_route history entries go 18 -> 36 across the whole run and the bound holds in practice -- growth is governed by body-pair count (3 corps x 6 unordered pairs), not by the 1496 deliveries, and the remaining 1464 ticks of traffic add nothing. Analytic ceiling is 2 x n(n-1)/2 per corp instead of n(n-1)/2. history_log_harness gained assertions for the pair, the distinct endpoint tags, the shared narration and tick, the deterministic order, and that a body-scoped filter finds the route from either side. AI_OPPONENT.md § 8a records the dual-endpoint contract, why not body_b, and the honest cost with its bound.
BL-282.summary: Ben, 2026-08-03 (NR-030): overturns my leave-as-is call. A newly established trade route is a two-body event, but `world_history_entry` carries one body tag; I tagged the destination and named both endpoints in the narration text, which meant a future 'show everything that happened at body X' filter would miss the route for its SOURCE body. Ben's call: push two entries, one tagged per endpoint.

BL-283.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-03 (Ben, NR-035 option a).

**The change.** Constrain Pass 3's anchor search window to the corporation's **home province**
rather than to its nation, and re-run `corp_terrain_matrix` against the narrower window.

**Why this rather than softening the wording.** Option (b) — rewording BL-219 to 'the province
it is registered in' — was available and cheaper, and is arguably the more realistic claim for
a large corporation with national reach. Ben chose the stronger behaviour instead: the province
should mean something spatially, not just categorically. That also makes the generated world
more legible — a corporation's holdings clustering where its history says it came from reads as
causal, whereas nation-wide scatter reads as arbitrary.

**What to watch when it lands.**

- **Placement failure.** A small or resource-poor home province may not contain a viable anchor
  for the corp's focus. Needs a documented fallback ladder — widen to adjacent provinces, then
  to the nation — rather than silently failing or placing nothing. The fallback must be
  deterministic.
- **`corp_terrain_matrix` shifts.** The matrix is derived from the search window, so narrowing
  the window changes it. Expect the corporation-mix goldens to move; re-bless deliberately and
  confirm every divergence is explicable, the way BL-218's harness moves were checked (NR-037).
- **Determinism.** The province window must be derived from already-deterministic state; no new
  RNG draw and no dependence on iteration order.

**Doc.** CORPORATION_GENERATION.md currently documents the gap honestly rather than implying the
stronger claim; when this lands, that note is replaced by the real behaviour and its fallback.
BL-283.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.10), implementing Ben's NR-035 option (a) as chosen -- the stronger behaviour, not the cheaper rewording. Pass 3's anchor search now runs over a HOME-PROVINCE window: the nation's tiles whose `nearest_province` is the corp's home province. Provinces are anchor points rather than stored tile sets, so nearest-anchor IS membership -- no new data structure was needed. The post-anchor neighbourhood walk deliberately stays nation-wide, so a small province spills next door rather than leaving the corp short. FALLBACK LADDER, each rung deterministic, and a rung that finds nothing consumes no RNG so widening is free in stream terms: (1) home province alone; (2) home province plus the 3 nearest same-nation provinces (column-wrapped anchor distance, ties to lower index); (3) whole nation, the old behaviour. HOW OFTEN IT FIRES, measured over 64 corps across 8 generations (seeds 0-5) rather than assumed: rung 1 89%, rung 2 0%, rung 3 11%. Every single rung-3 case was a corp with NO HOME PROVINCE AT ALL -- a nation the settlement pass never reached, which already falls back to national character for its focus. Where a home province exists it has never yet failed to host an anchor. Rung 2 is an unfired guard, kept because the cost is one sort and the failure it covers is real. TERRAIN MOVEMENT (seed 0, 18 holdings): barren 6->3, icy 5->3, grassland 3->7, forest 1->2, wetland 0->1. Holdings moved off dead ground onto settled ground, which is the causal read the item wanted -- provinces sit where people settled, so anchoring inside one pulls the corp onto habitable land. Cluster spread unchanged (mean max separation 1.2 tiles); 1.25 provinces per corp, 6 of 8 single-province. corp_terrain_matrix: exit 0, tier-1 FAILs 0, tier-2 WARNs 0. Only movement is body-wide free-tile counts (6084->6082, ports 1267->1265) and the player corp's richest reachable resource shifting iron_ore -> agricultural_produce, both downstream of holdings relocating. determinism_harness, world_determinism and settlement_harness byte-identical.
BL-283.summary: Ben, 2026-08-03 (NR-035): close the gap between BL-219's design claim and what shipped. The design says a corporation's focus follows 'the industrialisation history of the province it is anchored to'; as built, the corp picks a home province and derives its focus from it, but Pass 3 still places its starting holdings with the old nation-wide focus-scored anchor search. The province decides what the corp is; it does not yet decide where it is.

BL-284.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-03 (Ben, NR-036 option c — reopen as its own item, which subsumes option a's
assertion as this item's first task).

**Why this is not bookkeeping.** BL-218 chose the deeper, more expensive settlement-sim path
over a cheap alternative, and the single best argument for that choice was that fragmentation
would fall out of it for free. If it does not, the expensive path was bought on a promise that
did not pay — and nobody would currently know, because nothing counts exclaves.

**The measurement.** In `world_audit`, count each nation's **non-contiguous territorial
components** and attribute each one:

- **Emergent** — produced by the settlement sim itself (a growth front that crossed water and
  stalled, or was cut off by a rival's expansion). This is what the argument predicted.
- **Pass 2b** — assigned by orphan-island assignment, which still hands every water-disconnected
  component to its nearest nation. These are *authored*, not emergent, and must not be counted
  as evidence for the argument.

Report both counts per seed across the standard sweep, with the emergent share as the headline
number. Land the assertion with **wide** bars first and tighten once the real distribution is
known — the same discipline `mediterranean_sweep` used.

**What the result decides.**

- **Emergent exclaves appear at a reasonable rate** → the argument holds, BL-054's territorial
  half is genuinely complete, and this item closes having proved it.
- **They do not** → the fold was wrong and the territorial half needs real work: either Pass 2b
  stops absorbing every orphan, or the settlement sim needs a mechanism that lets a front stall
  across water. That work is filed then, against evidence, rather than guessed at now.

**Do not mark BL-054's territorial half complete until this closes.** That is the point of the
reopening.
BL-284.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.10). world_audit now counts each nation's non-contiguous territorial components over a 6-seed sweep and attributes each one. ATTRIBUTION IS EXACT, NOT HEURISTIC, which is what makes the answer trustworthy. Pass 2's BFS is water-blocked, so it only claims tiles on a landmass that already holds a seed, and there it runs to exhaustion -- therefore Pass 2b can only ever fire on a SEEDLESS landmass. So: exclave on a seeded landmass = emergent; on a seedless landmass = Pass 2b. No classifier, no threshold, no judgement call. THE ANSWER: 196 exclaves across the sweep -- 60 emergent, 136 Pass 2b. Emergent is 31% by COMPONENT COUNT but 49% by TILE COUNT (940 of 1930). Every seed produced emergent exclaves (6-17 each); roughly half of all nations hold at least one. THE VERDICT ON BL-218's PROMISE -- the reason this item exists. BL-218 bought the expensive settlement-sim path over a cheap alternative, and the single best argument for that choice was that fragmentation would fall out of it for free. IT PAYS, with a caveat about which number is quoted. The sim genuinely produces stalled fronts and rival cut-offs on every seed tested, and those are the LARGE exclaves. But Pass 2b's long tail of tiny orphan islands dominates the raw component count, so quoting '196 exclaves' would overstate the sim's contribution more than two-fold. THE TILE SHARE IS THE HONEST HEADLINE, and the audit prints both so the distinction cannot be lost. Nothing was tuned to make the answer nicer. The assertion is a deliberately wide bar (>= 6 emergent across the sweep, against 60 observed), to be tightened once the distribution has been watched rather than pinned to a first measurement. NATION_GENERATION.md gains a Territorial fragmentation, measured section, and its stale Pass 2c claim that fragmentation 'remains an open item' is corrected.
BL-284.summary: Ben, 2026-08-03 (NR-036): BL-054's territorial-fragmentation half is REOPENED as its own measurable item rather than being counted complete on the strength of BL-218's design argument. That argument — 'a real settlement sim produces exclaves for free; a growth front that crosses a strait and stalls leaves an exclave without anyone authoring one' — is what chose the expensive option over the cheap one. It has never been measured. Until it is, BL-054's territorial half is not complete.

BL-285.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-03 (Ben, NR-037 option b then c).

**Task 1 — GCC re-bless (do first, it is cheap).** BL-218/219 moved `ai_skill_harness`'s nine
MSVC assertions; those were re-blessed and verified against a stashed baseline as genuinely
caused by the change (every divergence upward — net worth up on seeds 0/2/4, dial counts past
the old ceiling on 0/1/4, solvency and survival in band on all five). The GCC set was not
re-run. Until it is, the two platforms' goldens describe different worlds, and the next
cross-platform failure will be ambiguous between a real regression and accumulated drift.
Re-run on Linux, confirm the divergences match the MSVC ones in direction, commit alongside.

**Task 2 — tag the ladder lines (the real fix).** `history_ladder_harness`'s H4 was **narrowed**
because it identifies its window by matching ladder line *text*. Narrowing made it pass; it did
not make it right — any rewording of a biography line still silently changes what H4 asserts
over, which is the failure mode a golden is supposed to catch rather than exhibit.

The fix: carry each ladder line's own `chain_stage` as a field, so H4 filters on the stage
rather than pattern-matching prose. Then restore H4 to its **stricter pre-narrowing form** —
the narrowing was a workaround for the fragility, so removing the fragility should remove the
need for it.

**Note the interaction with BL-283.** That item narrows Pass 3's placement window and expects
the corporation-mix goldens to move. Sequence the two so a golden is not re-blessed twice, and
so a move caused by BL-283 is not mistaken for platform drift.
BL-285.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.8). BOTH TASKS DONE. Task 1 — GCC re-bless: the Linux set had not been re-run since 2026-08-01 and failed 7 assertions across seeds 1/2/3. Re-blessed from a fresh Linux/GCC Release run; harness now ALL PASS. The divergence is DOWNWARD, unlike the MSVC re-bless of 2026-08-02 which was uniformly upward, and the explanation is recorded in the harness comment rather than waved through: BL-323's logistics reach rule bounds placement to ~77% of Kepler's land (a corp can no longer site on the richest tile regardless of remoteness) and BL-324's unit hiring adds a cash outflow that did not exist at the last bless (all five seeds show action[hire_unit]=21). Seed 1 fell 81% and went from highest of the five to lowest while seed 4 fell only 25% — a per-seed reshuffle is what a PLACEMENT constraint would produce, so the shape matches the cause. Survival held in band on all five: corps are poorer, not dying, which is the distinction between cost and collapse. Also flagged in the file: the MSVC set is now stale for the identical reason and will fail on the next Windows run; it must be re-blessed from a fresh MSVC run, never by copying the GCC numbers. Task 2 — ladder tagging: added `ladder_rung` (none/surplus/charter/borders) to history_event in planetology.hpp, a SECOND axis rather than more chain_stage values, since every ladder line sits at chain_stage::legacy and cannot be told apart by it. history_ladder.cpp tags its four emit sites. H4 now selects the three rungs structurally instead of matching the prose 'granary'/'Charter Act'/'Great Accord', so rewording a biography line can no longer silently change what H4 asserts over. Added an exactly-once-per-rung count check (surplus=1 charter=1 borders=1 verified) to stop a future duplicate emitter degrading the lookups. Note the scanned window is the whole recorded-history window — creeds and settlement write into it too and correctly carry rung::none — so counting tagged lines is the only exhaustiveness claim that is true there. history_ladder_harness ALL PASS. No serialisation impact: no save path exists yet.
BL-285.summary: Ben, 2026-08-03 (NR-037): two follow-ons from BL-218/219's harness moves, in order. (1) Re-run and re-bless the GCC golden set on the next Linux session — only the MSVC set was re-blessed, so the two platforms are currently drifting apart. (2) Tag history-ladder lines with their own `chain_stage` so H4 can filter on a field rather than text-match a line; text-matching is exactly the fragility that assertion had to be narrowed around.

BL-286.design:
DESIGNED 2026-08-04 (Ben brainstorm, filed retroactively after the code was already written on worktree-agent-a737ae8388a41f55b without a backlog entry — see NEEDS_REVIEW.json for the process note).

## The three axes

- **Flows, not stocks.** 0 A.D.'s four goods are banked and spent; a logistics system needs goods
  consumed every tick wherever a force is standing. Grain sets march radius; fodder is why
  animal-heavy forces stalled; salt converts a perishable good into a shippable one — its whole
  value is changing another good's logistics class, not being useful on its own.
- **Carrying capacity as a held resource.** transport_capacity is the single addition that most
  changes what a nation actor reasons about: pack animals/carts/hulls are built, lost, and
  captured, so effective supply range is capped by the train's own fodder draw rather than by a
  tuned constant.
- **Value density spread.** charcoal (very low — must be made beside the smelter), iron_blooms
  (medium — the material gate BL-274's era rosters assume), bullion (high — buy supply locally
  instead of hauling it, the real alternative to a train), trade_goods_misc (a placeholder slot
  for a specific endemic luxury — naming is a later step, per the mercantile track's BL-191
  precedent).

## What this item does NOT do

Enum + name-table + authored base price only. No mechanic reads these values yet:

- BL-287 (not yet filed): grain/fodder per-tick consumption draw.
- BL-288 (not yet filed): transport_capacity as a supply-range cap.
- BL-289 (not yet filed): salt as a ration shelf-life gate.
- BL-290 (not yet filed): bullion as a local-purchase mechanic.

## Naming

Plain English here for the reader (grain, salt, bullion). Per the standing rule
(io-standing-rules § Terms & docs), any in-sim/in-lore surfacing of these goods in the Era −1
sandbox (BL-271) uses the seeded name banks, not the English mechanism name — “grain” is the
mechanism, not the string.

## Process note

This item should have been filed BEFORE the enum change, per DELIVERY.md's lifecycle (Rule 0
item-spanning requirement gate). It was not — the code landed on a worktree branch with no
backlog entry. Filed retroactively at Ben's explicit confirmation (2026-08-04) to ship the enum
extension as-is. See NEEDS_REVIEW.json for the corresponding process entry.

CLOSED 2026-08-07 (cut audit, Ben approved). Scope was "enum + base-price wiring only" and that code shipped (components.hpp transport_capacity/iron_blooms/bullion). The unfiled follow-ons are owned by BL-295, this item's successor.
BL-286.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 from a Ben brainstorm about the 0 A.D. sandbox (Project-Rival, BL-271 era −1 proving ground): what other resources does a diverse, realistic logistics system need beyond food/wood/stone/metal? The answer organised around three axes rather than a longer stock list — per-tick flows (grain, fodder, water, salt), carrying capacity as a held resource (transport_capacity), and value density (charcoal, iron blooms, bullion, an endemic-luxury slot). Ben decided (2026-08-04) to ship these as a permanent extension of the shared resource_type enum — not a sandbox-local roster as first drafted — so resource_count moves from 23 to 31 and this IS a save-format retrofit (RESOURCES.md § Prototype scope). This item lands the enum values, name-lookup wiring, and authored placeholder base prices only; no consumption, transport-range cap, salt shelf-life gate, or bullion purchase mechanic reads them yet.

BL-302.design:
## Intent (design-owed)

Decide the dependency-acquisition posture rather than patch the symptom:

- **Local cache/mirror (likely cheapest):** seed FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SDL3 (or a shared FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR) from an existing build dir's _deps, so fresh worktrees configure offline. Pairs well with the worktree sub-agent model, which creates fresh dirs routinely.
- **Vendor:** commit the SDL3 source tarball; largest but removes the network from configure entirely.
- **Machine fix:** diagnose the schannel revocation failure (AV TLS interception vs cert-chain change); fragile, machine-specific.

Whichever lands, add the from-cold configure to a check so the regression is visible — NR-048's point is that green local build dirs hide this class of failure completely.
BL-302.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.8) — the POSTURE, which was the item's actual ask ('decide the dependency-acquisition posture rather than patch the symptom'). MEASUREMENT FIRST, and it overturned the item's own preferred option: a shared FETCHCONTENT_BASE_DIR HARD-FAILS across build trees, because each <dep>-subbuild carries a generator-locked CMakeCache ('Does not match the generator used previously'), and this checkout has build_gen, build_vs, build_linux and build_rel side by side. The item's other suggestion, per-dependency FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<dep>, works: sources shared, each tree keeps its own <dep>-build. CHOSEN AND IMPLEMENTED: ~98 additive lines in CMakeLists.txt resolve a cache dir (IO_DEPS_CACHE env var, else <source>/_deps_cache, the convention .gitignore already reserved) and then per dependency pick one of four branches — caller-supplied SOURCE_DIR is never second-guessed; an already-populated build tree is left completely alone (this is what protects build_linux); a populated cache seeds the source; otherwise it downloads cold as before. Each dependency is probed by a MARKER FILE, not a bare directory test, so a half-extracted cache is not accepted. No tarball vendored — unjustifiable against a fault that does not reproduce here and affects one machine. VISIBILITY, per the item's requirement: every configure now states its mode ('Deps: seeded from ... ' / 'Deps: COLD -> ...'), and DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md gains a Dependency acquisition section with the deliberate from-cold check (IO_DEPS_CACHE=/nonexistent is load-bearing in it — without that the cache seeds the check and it proves nothing). NOT VERIFIED, AND SAID SO: a from-cold configure SUCCEEDS on Linux in ~74s downloading ~120 MB, so the original Windows schannel TLS revocation failure does not reproduce here and remains unproven either way. Carried by BL-341 (run the from-cold check on Windows). The cache is also opt-in: it does nothing until someone runs the seed command, so a fresh clone still downloads once.
BL-302.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 off NR-048, upgraded from observation after the recommended retry REPRODUCED it (curl to codeload.github.com fails TLS, exit 35; CMake reports "unable to check revocation for the certificate" in FetchContent_MakeAvailable(SDL3), CMakeLists.txt:44). Existing build dirs are unaffected (populated _deps), which hides it — but a fresh clone, a new git worktree, or a CI runner cannot configure at all, and it blocked BL-287's from-cold timing measurement. Candidate fixes: vendor the dep, point FetchContent at a local cache/mirror (FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SDL3), or settle the machine's schannel revocation posture. Check CI first: if CI provisions fresh dirs it may already be red.

BL-305.design:
## Intent (design-owed)

Questions the design must settle:
1. **Live or replay?** Show the carve as it generates (generation-screen stage, BL-256's globe as the surface) or as a post-hoc scrubbable replay (Generation Ledger sibling)? The BFS is deterministic and fast, so both are cheap; the difference is where the player is standing.

## SETTLED 2026-08-08 (Ben)

- **The corp-seeding step gets both surfaces, split by kind**: asset placement renders spatially on the canvas/globe (it's positional, so the canvas is where it belongs); financial-profile derivation surfaces as a card/ledger entry (it isn't positional, so a canvas overlay would be the wrong shape for it).
- The coverage-check task (walk GENERATION_STRATEGY.md's pass map, note any step still invisible-by-design) stays in scope as the item's closing step, unchanged.

BL-308.design: Filed 2026-08-06, from the strategy-library design session (docs/ai/STRATEGIES.md). BL-308.resolution: Landed 2026-08-09 (v0.1.10). `resource_type::propellant = 31`, count 31 -> 32. BL-316.design:
## What the investigation found

**1. Supply's entire dynamic range is 10% of combat power.** In combat.cpp supply only mitigates ATTRITION, and attrition is `terrain_attrition x season`. With a null terrain view every battle resolves on grassland/plains, where attrition is 100/1000. So fully supplied costs 0% and TOTALLY CUT OFF costs 10%. That is noise against roster modifiers, and it is why a province 34 tiles away was taken at 5% supply in the vacuous-stall test (pre-rebase id BL-312, since reassigned; landed 2026-08-05, 'Four review items').

**2. The terrain module is inert.** Both callers (the sweep and the Ages view) pass `sim_terrain_view{}`. A mountain battle would carry up to 900/1000 attrition and supply would matter enormously - but no Era -1 battle has ever been fought on real ground.

**3. There is no cost of breadth at all.** Not weak - absent. No upkeep, no administrative drag, no garrison burden, no distance-from-capital penalty on holdings.

## Three slices

**S1 - real terrain.** Build the terrain view from the body's tiles and pass it. Nearly free, makes terrain_combat live, and sharpens everything the sweep measures.

**S2 - terrain-weighted reach.** Replace Chebyshev distance-from-capital with a cost computed over the neighbour graph using the landform traversal costs logistics.cpp already defines (plains 1.0 -> mountain 2.0). Computed by Dijkstra from the capital and cached until the capital changes, so the per-year cost stays a lookup.

**S3 - the burden of breadth.** Supply available to any campaign falls with the polity's total holdings. This is the mechanism Ben asked for and the one BL-277's (Era -1 military strategy) answered Q2 wrongly claimed already existed - an answer that now survives only in the 2026-08-05 commits, since the 2026-08-07 rebase dropped it from the item's design prose. With it, the frontier stall becomes arithmetic rather than a `w_dist` scoring preference.

## Why this is priority A

It is the missing physical constraint under three open findings. The no-elimination finding (nobody is ever eliminated; pre-rebase id BL-308, reassigned by the 2026-08-07 rebase; retired as a standalone item by Ben's same-day ruling - the target, elimination possible and subject-nation release possible, is recorded on BL-271) and BL-277's (Era -1 military strategy) corrected Q2 (the stall is a preference, not a limit; the correction lives in the 2026-08-05 review commit) both trace back to expansion being free. Empires grow without limit because nothing charges them for size.
BL-316.summary: Filed 2026-08-04 from Ben's question: 'how is logistics factored into our generation? Three real logistics systems exist (logistics.cpp's terrain-weighted A* with road discounts, supply_system, road_generation) and the Era -1 sim uses NONE of them; its supply is one line of straight-line Chebyshev distance. Worse, the sim passes a NULL terrain view, so every battle in every run is fought on default grassland/plains and the whole terrain_combat module (including BL-233's modifiers) is inert. And there is no per-holding cost of any kind: holding 500 provinces costs exactly what holding 5 costs.

BL-321.design:
## The shape - mirror unit_roster, do NOT reuse building_component

This is BL-274's sibling on the noun axis, and it copies that item's settled shape verbatim: an **authored C++ table**, four bands (reuse `roster_band`), rows gated on the province endowment windows the settlement pass already computes, availability **derived from the ground** - no research, no unlock events, no player choice.

**It must not reuse `building_component`** (components.hpp:252). That struct is the campaign-era building: a tile entity carrying a recipe index, a workforce target, an auto-solver flag, credit/resource build cost, per-tick maintenance and wages, decommission state and construction ticks. Era -1 has no credits, no market, no recipe registry and no economy tick - it has a year loop over provinces. Sharing the struct would drag the whole campaign economy into the generation layer to satisfy fields nothing sets. A work is instead a small id held by the *province*, not an entity on a tile.

## Storage: C++ table, not Lua (decision taken 2026-08-07, see NR)

The campaign era authors building data in Lua (`scripts/economy.lua` -> `building_economics`, `scripts/recipes.lua` -> the recipe registry), and TECH_FOUNDATIONS names 'building definitions' as a sanctioned scripting-boundary. That precedent does **not** carry here. `recipe_registry.cpp` is the *one* TU in the project that pulls sol2/Lua; every other `src/world/*.cpp` is deliberately SDL/Lua-free so the headless harnesses build with nothing but a C++20 compiler (TECH_FOUNDATIONS.md:142-145). The Era -1 sim is verified exclusively by those harnesses (`history_sweep.cpp`, `history_sim_harness.cpp`). Putting the works table in Lua would either drag Lua into the headless world layer or force a second loading path for the same data.

So: **authored C++ table in `works_roster.cpp`**, exactly as `unit_roster.cpp` does. Lua keeps the campaign-era balance data it already owns. If the works table ever needs live retuning, the right move is to promote it *with* the unit roster, once, not to split the two.

## Rows

`work_row { const char* name; roster_band band; work_gate gate; work_effect effect; int weight; }`

`work_gate` reuses the `roster_gate` axes (ore_q / farm_q / port_q / energy_q, 0-1000 thresholds, zero = no gate) plus a population floor - a granary needs people before it needs grain.

`work_effect` deltas ONLY quantities the sim already has, per-mille:

- `capacity_mod` - the province's demographic carrying capacity (BL-273's logistic ceiling).
- `manpower_mod` - the manpower ceiling, i.e. what the province can raise.
- `reach_mod` - a discount on the terrain-weighted supply cost through/from this province. **This is the row that matters**: it is how a polity buys its way past BL-316 S3's burden of breadth.
- `defence_mod` - a modifier the province contributes to `army_stack_entry` when defending, resolved through combat.cpp's existing terrain path. Never a new combat concept.
- `industrial_mod` - pull-forward on the Stage 4 furnace date.

First-cut roster, generic mechanism nouns only (standing naming rule - no Earth proper noun, and none of these may read as recognisably Latin):

| Band | Rows |
|---|---|
| Classical | Granary, Channel Works, Ore Pits, Wall Circuit, Way Station, Harbour Mole |
| Medieval | Water Mill, Stone Fortress, Guild Quarter, Deepwater Wharf, Span Bridge |
| Gunpowder | Bastion Fort, Powder Mill, Counting House, Cut Canal, Naval Yard |
| Industrial | Blast Works, Rail Head, Signal Line, Arsenal, Coaling Station |

Bands are cumulative for the same reason the roster's are: nothing un-invents a granary.

## Who builds, and when

The sim's existing per-year polity scorer (BL-318's shared-currency verbs) gains a `build_work` verb priced in the same currency as its campaign verbs, so building a Way Station competes directly with raising an army - which is the whole point. A work is chosen by score over the available rows, paid in the shared currency, and recorded as a dated `history_event` line so it lands in the chronicle.

## What it hands the campaign (the BL-272 parity contract)

Industrial-band works are the **ancestors of `building_type`**. A province that lit Blast Works in 1780 is where the 1960 smelter sits and why its substrate density is high. Landing this closes a real gap in `substrate_density`, which is currently generated rather than earned. Scope fence: this item **records** the correspondence; consuming it in campaign generation is a follow-on, not a slice here.

## Slices

- **S1** - `works_roster.{hpp,cpp}`: the table, the gate check, `available_works(province, band)`. Pure, headless-testable, no sim changes. Mirrors unit_roster's own first cut.
- **S2** - province storage: a small `std::vector<uint8_t>` (or bitmask) of built work ids on `province`, plus the effect accumulators the sim reads.
- **S3** - the `build_work` verb in the scorer, priced in the shared currency; dated history lines.
- **S4** - wire `reach_mod` into BL-316's terrain-weighted reach and `defence_mod` into the combat path; re-run the sweep and report whether the frontier stall moved from ceiling to decision.

## Sequencing

**Requires BL-316 (Era -1 logistics) to land first.** S4 has nothing to discount until terrain-weighted reach exists, and the item's whole justification is the counter-move to BL-316 S3. Filed priority A for that coupling, not for urgency against v0.1.1 - ROADMAP.md owns the sequence.

## S1 landed 2026-08-07 (same session as filing)

src/world/works_roster.{hpp,cpp} + tools/verify/works_roster_harness.cpp — the table (21 rows across the four bands), the gate check, available_works, work_id and total_work_effect. 22 assertions PASS over R1-R7. Pure and standalone: no sim change, no province-struct change, nothing wired. CMake needs no edit (both source lists are GLOB CONFIGURE_DEPENDS).

R7 is the assertion worth keeping: every reach-bearing work must be gateable by some ground, AND an endowment-poor province must still be able to raise one. Without that second half, poor ground has no way to buy reach and BL-316 S3 stays a ceiling rather than a decision — the exact failure this item exists to prevent.

S2-S4 remain, and S4 is still gated on BL-316 (era -1 logistics): reach_mod has nothing to discount until terrain-weighted reach exists.

## S2-S4 landed 2026-08-13

**S2 — province storage.** `province::works_built` is a 32-bit MASK plus five plain-int
accumulators (`work_capacity_mod` .. `work_industrial_mod`), not the vector the design
offered: the struct is copied on every Settle and lives in a vector that grows past 400 entries
inside a pass already costing ~23 s of a ~25 s world, so heap ownership per province was the
wrong trade. Plain ints rather than a `work_effect` member because works_roster.hpp
forward-declares `province` — including it back would close a cycle to store five numbers.
The mask imposes a 32-row ceiling, now checked by the loader (a 33rd row would validate and then
be unbuildable). `apply_work_to_province` maintains the accumulators incrementally and REFUSES
a double build, which is what makes a province’s works a finite, saturating investment.

**S3 — the `build_work` verb.** A fifth scored candidate in BL-309’s shared currency, priced in
the ROUND it consumes rather than in a treasury Era -1 does not have. A work’s benefit splits by
who receives it: local effects against the province’s own endowment, reach against the polity’s
MEAN holding (against the total it was worth ~40x every local effect and the roster collapsed to
its five road rows). Bounded to two candidate provinces per polity per round — capital plus one
rotated by a hash of (polity, year, slot) — because scoring every holding is O(held x rows) in the
sim’s hot loop. Band keyed off MATERIALS capacity, not military.

**S4 — the consumers.** Every effect axis reaches something real: `capacity_mod` into a new
`province_carrying_capacity(farm_q, mod)` overload that raises the logistic ASYMPTOTE (and into
the Settle verb’s pressure test, which must divide by the same K); `manpower_mod` into
`manpower_ceiling(pop, mod)` read by `replenish_manpower`; `reach_mod` into BOTH the staging
hub’s terrain-cost discount (scorer and execution, which must agree) and the polity’s mean relief
on BL-314’s burden of breadth; `defence_mod` into defender readiness via `roster_stack`, and
into the scorer so a polity does not walk into an unseen bastion.

**One recorded divergence: `industrial_mod`.** The design calls it a pull-forward on the Stage 4
furnace date, which is not implementable — Stage 4 runs in `run_settlement`, finished before this
loop starts. Wired instead to the capacity ladder, which is what the sim actually has as an
industrial clock. NR-195 records the call.

**Wiring.** `run_history_sim` and `make_hard_coded_world` both take a defaulted
`const works_registry*`; app loads the table before generation via a new idempotent
`ensure_works_loaded()` (it previously loaded inside `load_economy`, which runs AFTER
`setup_world` — generation would have seen an empty table; NR-196).

**Verification.** `history_sweep` carries the roster on every run, reports works-raised per
world, and gates W1..W7: endowment gates fire and poor ground still gets a reach work, the
population floor gates independently, bands gate and stay cumulative, a work applies once and
refuses twice, the accumulators agree with a fresh recompute, capacity works leave a world
carrying more people, a null registry disables the verb entirely, two runs at one seed raise the
same works on the same provinces, and pre-built reach measurably changes the supply path.
