## Why this is its own item, and why it is first

Appending a `resource_type` value stopped being free on 2026-08-22, when the save format landed: every per-resource array is sized off `resource_count`, so an append changes every array length and is a format break. `components.hpp` says so at the enum.

Doing it once, deliberately, ahead of the roster work keeps the rest of the sprint out of `world_save.cpp` entirely.

**Sequencing is load-bearing.** Sprint 16 bumps `world_save_version` (3 → 4) in three of its own items. This item takes the NEXT number and must not begin until Sprint 16 has merged to main (Ben’s sequencing ruling, 2026-08-23). Starting early means two sprints minting the same version number for different formats.

## Work

1. Append the goods the wide roster needs, at the END of the enum, never inserted. First cut, each earning its place by being consumed by an authored recipe in BL-586 (the admission rule, PRODUCTION.md): `hides`, `leather`, `cloth`, `ceramics`, `tools`, `dressed_stone`, `planks`. Seven values; the exact set is settled WITH BL-586’s chains, not before — a good with no consumer does not get in.
2. `world_gen.lua` `base_price` for each. Price is DERIVED from the input basket at the processing roster’s observed output:input ratio, not picked — `recipes.lua`’s note at the ordnance entry states the method.
3. `world_save_version` bump, and the read path’s strict-equality rejection. No migration of old saves: the header exists precisely to refuse a mismatch (`world_save.hpp`).
4. `chain_depth`’s R1/R1b rows re-run — every new value must be obtainable AND wanted in the same band, or it does not ship.

BL-286 put eleven goods in the enum with their behaviours “unfiled”; five were deleted twelve days later, having been produced by nothing and consumed by nothing. That deletion is why `resource_type` is clean today. Nothing here lands ahead of its consumer.

BL-586.design:
## The pattern, restated because it is the whole method

A named building is a recipe, or an extraction target, on a generic `building_type` — distinguished by placement rule and glyph, not by an enum value. Mint a new `building_type` only where BL-325’s test is met: a distinct placement rule AND a distinct glyph AND behaviour no recipe can express. The military base passed that test. A tannery does not.

## The chains to author

Each line is a named building; each declares its group (BL-434, sub-facility groups) and its `era = "ancient"` tag. Depths follow from the graph and are never authored:

| Building | Chain | Group |
|---|---|---|
| Tannery | hides → leather | Artisan Goods |
| Weaver | (split out of Potter & Weaver) fibre → cloth | Artisan Goods |
| Potter | clay → ceramics | Artisan Goods |
| Sawmill | timber → planks | Construction Materials (new group) |
| Stonemason | stone → dressed_stone | Construction Materials |
| Toolmaker | iron_blooms + planks → tools | Metal Foundry |
| Shipwright | planks + cloth → a terminal trade good | Advanced Fabrication |

`hides` comes from a pasture / hunting extraction target — the endemic `furs` tier already proves that extraction shape works.

The exact list is content work and will move at authoring. The **admission rule is the invariant**: no building whose output nothing consumes, no good no building consumes. `chain_depth`’s R1/R1b enforces it, and must be green at the end of every slice, not only at the end of the item.

## Depth is the point, not a side effect

Ancient max depth is **3** today, on one chain (timber → charcoal → blooms → steel). A roster that is wide and FLAT is twenty ways to do the same shallow thing — BL-429’s slice-1 note says exactly this, and it is the trap to avoid. Every chain above should reach depth 2 or better; the Toolmaker (blooms + planks) is deliberately the deepest, at 4.

## Glyphs

`icons::building()` keys off the identity resource — an extraction site’s target, a processing facility’s primary output — so each NEW GOOD needs a glyph, not each new building. Two buildings reaching the same good share one by design (ICONS.md § 1c). Budget: one glyph per BL-585 value.

## Owed alongside the code

Placement rules for any target that is not simply “has a deposit”; `k_extractable` updated for every new extraction target — BL-429 slice 2 found `peat` authored on tiles but missing from that array, so no site could ever have targeted it; and PRODUCTION.md § The ancient chain rewritten to the new table.

Four named buildings on EXISTING raws, no new deposit or extraction target: Potter's Kiln (clay -> ceramics), Stonemason (stone -> dressed_stone), Sawmill (timber -> planks), Toolmaker (iron_blooms + planks -> tools, required depth 2, so depth(tools) = 3 - tied with the existing ancient ceiling, not past it as originally hoped). Construction Materials is a new BL-434 group (the Kiln, Stonemason, Sawmill); Toolmaker joined Metal Foundry as its deepest member. chain_depth R1/R1b/R2 all green; recipe_switch_harness, price_band_harness, save_roundtrip, determinism_harness, spectator_determinism all rerun clean; full tree (cmake --build build, every target) compiles with zero errors.

**Deliberately NOT this slice** (the remainder of the table above): Tannery/hides->leather, Weaver/hides->cloth, Shipwright/planks+cloth->trade good. All three need a new extractable raw (hides) with real tile-generation deposits - a materially bigger change (new terrain-generation deposit authoring, not just a recipe) than this slice's four, deliberately deferred rather than rushed. Also not this slice: placement_rules.cpp and icons.cpp - none of the four new buildings are extraction sites (no k_extractable entry needed), and icons::building()'s default fallback (a generic square/ore-chunk) renders them without a crash, same precedent as BL-429's own slice 1 (identities before glyphs).

## SLICE 2 LANDED 2026-08-24 — item complete

Five new resource_type values (hides, fibre, leather, cloth, rigging; resource_count 42 -> 47) complete the table: Tannery (hides -> leather), Weaver (fibre -> cloth), Shipwright (planks + cloth -> rigging, Advanced Fabrication group, the roster's first depth-2 chain). Both new raws registered in placement_rules::k_extractable so they're reachable end to end (the four pre-existing endemic goods share that same gap, left unfixed as out of scope). world_save_version bumped 9 -> 10 (structural). All mechanical seams repeated (components.hpp, resource_names.cpp, verify_api.cpp slugs, presentation.cpp resource_table, world_gen.lua prices, economy.lua material overrides, icons.cpp glyphs). A real regression surfaced and ruled on: resource_count's widening shifted an RNG stream and broke spectator_determinism's R1 A/B family-coverage check, unrelated to the new content (differentially proven). Ben ruled that check retired rather than patched — see NR-596 and io-standing-rules.md's BL-409 section for the scope of what the harness still guarantees. BL-587.design:
## What was measured, and what it corrects

PRODUCTION.md § Alternate production methods still reports four dominated sibling pairs as “Ben’s open call (NR-243)”. **That text is stale.** The guard that found them was retracted on 2026-08-16 and replaced: `recipe_switch_harness.cpp` records the retraction in its own header, and `chain_depth.cpp`’s R2 is the replacement.

All four were false positives of grouping by (primary output, era band). `steel_from_iron_nickel` vs `steel`, `peat_charcoal` vs `charcoal` and `glass` vs `trade_goods` have **disjoint raws** — which one a corp runs is decided by deposit access, not by price. The propellant pair is an explicitly named atmosphere-versus-airless precondition.

The live consequence is the opposite of a balance defect: with every pair bucketed as a route or an exemption, **no pair is a method at all**, and the no-dominance rule has nothing to guard.

## What an interchangeable method actually is

Two recipes on one building, sharing at least one input, either of which a corp on a given tile could genuinely run. Ben, 2026-08-23: *“it’s not always clear that a more advanced method is better (depending on which market it builds to).”* So the axis is which market the output is going to, not which route is stronger:

  * **Ratio** — a Bloomery and a larger furnace both take `iron_ore + charcoal`, differing in fuel-per-unit against throughput. Cheap fuel favours one, cheap ore the other.
  * **Yield split** — a method with a second, lesser output: worth more where that byproduct has a market, worthless where it does not.
  * **Labour against materials** — a hand method cheap to build and dear to run; the powered one inverts it. Note the constraint: `base_wage` lives on `building_economics`, keyed by TYPE, so this axis needs the rate on the recipe or the cost on the named building (BL-590) — there is no wage per method today.

First cut: **three** genuine method pairs, at least one of them ancient, each authored with the market condition under which it wins stated in a comment beside it.

## The guard must grow with the content

R2 compares one fixed reference-price snapshot. A method that is only better “depending on which market it builds to” is invisible to a single snapshot — it will read as dominated. R2 gains a second price vector, and asserts each genuine method wins under at least one. That is the mechanical form of the ruling; the guard work itself is BL-592.

## What this item deliberately does NOT do

It deletes nothing. The 2026-08-23 ruling to “delete the dominated sibling” was taken on the stale doc text above, and the four pairs it names are not dominated. Deleting them would remove the coal Smelter, the Charcoal Burner, the Potter & Weaver and the airless propellant route for no measured reason — and would strand `sand`, `peat` and `iron_nickel_ore` as orphans, failing R1 in the same pass. Recorded as a correction rather than acted on; re-rule if the deletion is still wanted.

PRODUCTION.md corrected — NR-243 closed rather than retuned (NR-589).

So the 2026-08-15 ruling ("alternates with real trade-offs") is mechanism without content: the Method page offers siblings, but no two of them are a choice a corp can actually make on one tile. BL-588.design:
## The measurement

`tech_effect_kind` is `unlock_structure` | `modify_scalar` (`tech_gate.hpp`). `prototype_tech_gates()` returns **one** gate. `scripts/tech_tree.lua` opens with *DATA ONLY — the tech system is post-prototype; nothing in the simulation reads this.* So the only earned lock in the economy today is `depth_locked`, and it applies only to recipes tagged `era = "ancient"`.

## Work

1. A third arm, `tech_effect_kind::unlock_recipe`, carrying a recipe **name** — not an id. Recipe ids are positional and stored in `building_component.recipe`; a gate that outlives a roster edit must not silently repoint. Mirror field alongside `unlocks_structure`, authored only through `add_effect`, exactly as the existing arms are.
2. `recipe_unlocked(w, corp, recipe_id)` beside `structure_unlocked`.
3. **Read at both doors**, exactly as the depth gate is: `construct_building` guards placement, `try_switch_recipe` guards retooling. Guarding only placement leaves the one-click bypass the depth gate already documents — place the shallow method, then retool onto the gated sibling in the same group.
4. `construction_result::tech_locked` and `recipe_switch_result` gain the recipe case; `corp_command_result::rejected_tech_locked` is reused, so an agent cannot tell a structure lock from a recipe lock on the seam. The three locks stay distinct in MEANING, and that distinction is already documented: `era_locked` never available, `tech_locked` earned by research, `depth_locked` earned by building.
5. **The Build door and the scorer must filter on it.** `corp_ai.cpp` walks the whole processing roster picking best net margin, filtering on era and depth only; an unfiltered tech-locked recipe would have every rival scoring a candidate the seam then refuses. The door filters for the same reason it filters depth — the door does not offer what the gate would refuse.
6. Author the gates: a first cut across BL-586’s chains, predicates written in `condition_set` against what a corp has already DONE — structures held, goods produced, surplus — never a timer.

## The design constraint Ben set

This is not a reshaping of the tech tree; the ~150 nodes stay as they are. What changes is that some of them resolve. And an unlocked method is **not a strict upgrade** (BL-587): earning it opens a different trade, so the tree expresses progression without expressing power.
BL-588.resolution: Third tech_effect_kind arm, unlock_recipe, storing a recipe name (never an id). Checked at both doors: construct_building (returns the existing construction_result::tech_locked) and try_switch_recipe (new recipe_switch_result::tech_locked, mapped to the existing corp_command_result::rejected_tech_locked). corp_ai.cpp's build-candidate loop filters on it. Two first-cut gates authored fresh (E0-EC-01 Toolmaker, E1-EC-01 Bessemer Converter) rather than transcribed from tech_tree.lua's unreviewed node list (NR-591). E1-EC-01's first predicate (surplus only) was caught by tech_gate_harness's own T3 fixture as satisfiable by any solvent corp regardless of what it had built; corrected to require holding machinery in stockpile. Full tree build and 12 relevant harnesses (tech_effect_union_harness, tech_gate_harness, construction_gate_harness, construction_harness, corp_ai_harness, chain_depth, recipe_switch_harness, price_band_harness, save_roundtrip, determinism_harness, spectator_determinism, corp_ai_predictive_harness, corp_agency_harness) all clean; spectator_determinism's golden held with no re-bless needed.
BL-588.summary: Ben, 2026-08-23: "include the notion of progression in different methods ... most building types, and most recipes are not buildable on game start." Measured: tech_effect has exactly two arms — unlock a building_type, or move a scalar — so a tech cannot reach a recipe at all. And exactly ONE gate is authored (E0-ML-01, the military base) against ~150 inert nodes in tech_tree.lua, which says of itself that nothing in the simulation reads it. This item adds the arm, and enough authored gates that the roster is earned rather than handed over.

BL-589.design:
## What a fresh ancient corp sees today

The Build door collapses processing to one row per GROUP (BL-434), so an ancient campaign shows four processing rows — Metal Foundry, Food Processing, Fuel Production, Artisan Goods — plus one extraction row per extractable deposit on the tile, plus four infrastructure rows. Of those, only Metal Foundry’s ancient members are depth-gated, and even that group stays visible because its representative can be an `any`-band recipe (`refined_copper`), which the depth filter deliberately never touches.

## Work

1. **A stated opening set.** Name the buildings a corp may place at tick 0 — first cut: extraction, one food route, one fuel route. Everything else is earned, by depth (BL-586’s chains) or by tech (BL-588’s gates).
2. **Re-check the `any`-band escape.** An `any`-band recipe is never depth-filtered, per the 2026-08-16 first-cut ruling. With a wide ancient roster that exemption becomes load-bearing in the wrong direction — it is how a group stays open when all its ancient members are locked. Either the ancient band gets its own representative selection, or the exemption narrows. State the call; do not let it stand as a default.
3. **The assertion**, in `chain_depth`: at reached depth 0 with no techs earned, the count of placeable ancient buildings is at or below the authored opening set — and every one of the rest is reachable by SOME sequence. The no-stranded-recipe row already present, applied to the opening rather than to the ceiling.

## The failure this guards against

A narrow opening that is narrow because something is unreachable is worse than a wide one. `chain_depth` already states the principle: an unplaceable building is the roster’s orphan. Both halves — few at the start, all of them eventually — must be asserted together, or tuning will satisfy one by breaking the other.
BL-589.resolution: Measured (live-Lua probe): five processing groups open at tick 0, wider than the item's own first-cut guess. Put five concrete calls to Ben via elicitation form; the ruling closed only Metal Foundry (refined_copper, an any-band recipe with no ancient identity and no depth gate — the roster's widest anachronism) behind a new tech gate, E0-EC-03, and left Fuel Production, Food Processing, Artisan Goods and Construction Materials exactly as measured. chain_depth's new G5 row asserts the ruled opening exactly (4/4) and confirms E0-EC-03 is not a permanent orphan. Full tree build + 11 harnesses clean, spectator_determinism golden held. A real coverage gap found and recorded, not fixed: tech_gate_harness only exercises the original garrison gate directly; the three economy gates are proven correct only indirectly across other harnesses (NR-594).
BL-589.summary: Ben, 2026-08-23: "most building types, and most recipes are not buildable on game start." Measured against that: of the eight building types only the launchpad (era) and the military base (tech) are withheld, and of the eight ancient recipes only the Bloomery chain sits above required depth 0 — so a fresh ancient corp is offered nearly the whole roster in its first minute. This item makes the opening narrow, and asserts it.

BL-590.design:
## The shape of the change

`resource_build_cost` stays where it is as the DEFAULT for a type. What is added is an override keyed by the named building — the pair that already identifies one everywhere else in the codebase:

  * extraction: `(building_type, target_resource)`
  * processing: `(building_type, recipe)`

Authored in `economy.lua` beside the type’s own entry. Absent means the type default, so nothing that does not opt in changes.

## Where it is read

Eight call sites across five files read `econ.resource_build_cost` directly today: `construction.cpp` (the real gate), `economy_system.cpp` (three — the per-tick material draw during construction), `selection_panel.cpp` (the Build door’s capex figure, and the road path), `construction_panel.cpp`. Every one goes through a single lookup, for the reason BL-436 records about richness: **a preview that disagrees with the tick prices a building the economy will not deliver.** The door’s `capex` and `material_rate` are previews of exactly this number.

## What it buys, beyond flavour

A second sink for the shallow goods. Timber, stone, clay and dressed stone become things a corp needs because it is BUILDING, not only because a recipe consumes them — which is the demand that makes an early quarry worth owning. It also gives the depth ladder a second bite: a deep building can cost a deep good.

## Watch

`corp_ai.cpp` prices candidates through the same estimate, so the scorer picks the change up for free — but a building whose materials a corp cannot reach becomes a candidate it will score and then fail to place. Check the candidate filter; do not assume it.
BL-590.resolution: resource_build_cost_for(type, target, recipe) is the single lookup every material-cost call site now goes through (13 occurrences across 4 files migrated). extraction_site keyed by target_resource, processing_facility by recipe id, falling back to the type default when unauthored. First-cut coverage: the whole ancient roster (5 extraction targets, 13 processing recipes) gets a timber/stone basket instead of steel; industrial/space-sourced entries unchanged. Verified three ways: construction_harness R9 (hand-built registry, 5/5), full tree build + 10 harnesses clean, and a live-Lua probe confirming the authored economy.lua tables actually resolve (built, run, deleted). A real pre-existing gap found and recorded rather than silently fixed: corp_ai.cpp's build-candidate scoring never prices resource_build_cost, only build_cost — filed as NR-592, not this item's scope to close.
BL-590.summary: RULING 2026-08-23 (Ben): materials vary per named building. Measured: resource_build_cost sits on building_economics, which is keyed by building_type, so all eight types cost steel and nothing else — the launchpad alone adds refined fuel. An ancient world whose every structure is smelted steel is the same anachronism the launchpad’s era tag was written to remove, and it leaves timber, stone, clay and the BL-585 goods with one recipe sink apiece and no construction sink at all.

BL-591.design:
## The question the surface answers (BL-260 discipline)

**“How far down the production graph has my company actually got, and what does the next rung open?”**

It is a corporation-grain fact — `corp_reached_depth` reads `corporation_component::produced_ever` — which is why the building card was the wrong home for it and the dashboard is the right one. The 2026-08-15 rework cut it for the right reason; the idea was not what was wrong.

## Content

Three lines, no more:

1. **Reached depth**, and the good that set it — the deepest thing the corp has ever made. Produced-once-ever, never cleared, so the number only rises.
2. **What the next rung opens** — the buildings whose `recipe_required_depth` is exactly `reached + 1`.
3. **What is missing to get there** — the input those recipes need that the corp has never produced. This is the line that turns a lock into an instruction.

## Constraints

The dashboard is four cards with an in-place expansion and a full-canvas takeover (BL-265). This is a Production-card concern rather than a fifth card — confirm on sight, not by argument. Rule 0b applies: state the current measurements before reshaping, and open the live app before asking Ben to judge it.

A rival’s reached depth is **private** and must not appear. The Method and Profitability pages are already withheld from a rival card for exactly this reason, and under spectator god view the rule is sight, never hands.

## Owed alongside the code

`question_log.json` entry written WITH the surface, not after. A user story on the intent axis — there is nothing on “know how far my production has reached” today. No `ACTIONS.json` entry: this is a readout, not a control.

**A live click before the visual requirement is marked complete**, per the standing rule — a capture proves it renders, not that the card is reachable.

## Rows

1. **R2 gains a second price vector.** Today it compares one fixed reference snapshot, which cannot see a method that is better “depending on which market it builds to” (Ben, 2026-08-23) — such a method reads as dominated. Two vectors, fuel-cheap and fuel-dear; a genuine interchangeable method must win under at least one. A method that wins under neither is dead content and fails the row.
2. **The start-gate row** (BL-589): at reached depth 0 with no techs earned, placeable ancient buildings are at or below the authored opening set — AND every withheld one is reachable by some sequence. Both halves or neither; a narrow opening bought with an unreachable building is worse than a wide one.
3. **A materials row** (BL-590): every named building’s material basket is obtainable in its own band. A quarry costing a good only the industrial arc makes is unbuildable at 0 CE, and nothing else in the suite would catch it.
4. **R1/R1b re-run** across BL-585’s appends. The rows already exist, but they ARE the sprint’s admission rule and should be named in its requirement rather than assumed to still pass.

## Why not a new harness

`chain_depth` already owns the recipe graph, loads the shipped Lua, and holds the roster invariants. A second harness would need a second reference-price table and would give two answers to one question — which is the stated reason R1 was moved OUT of `recipe_switch_harness` in the first place. Grow the one that owns it.

Naming the new rows in `.claude/skills/verifier-headless/SKILL.md` is part of this item, not a follow-up (CLAUDE.md § Tool creation is skill creation).

## The playthrough

One session, played end to end, each step written down as it happens:

1. A fresh ancient corp is offered the authored opening set and no more (BL-589).

A step that only works because the harness says so. The standing rule is explicit: a scripted capture proves a surface renders, not that a press on it is reachable. Every UI step above is a live click.

BL-598.design:
## Ben's words
> "Province selection element must be bundled into the tile selection element. By this I
> mean, we just use a longer accordion. We can also swap the order. Buildings -> Deposits ->
> Resources -> Population -> Terrain. Keep the tile available buildings tab, and drop the
> province buildings tab."

## What changes
Today the band shows a province card and a tile card as two separate kinds, each with its own
paged centre pane - 'Terrain (1/3)', 'Tiles (1/3)' - stepped with prev/next arrows. This
replaces the pair with ONE element and swaps the pager idiom for an accordion, ordered
**Buildings, Deposits, Resources, Population, Terrain**. That order is itself the argument:
it runs from what the player can act on to what the ground merely is, where the pager's order
ran the other way.

The tile's available-buildings tab stays. The province buildings tab goes - it was the same
question asked at a grain the player does not build at.

## The call this needs
SELECTION.md's repeat-click cycle is battle, unit, province, building, tile. If the province
is a SECTION of the tile element rather than a kind of its own, does the cycle still stop at
a province rung, or does that rung dissolve? Dissolving it is the cleaner reading of 'bundled
into', and it costs the only gesture that selects a province without selecting a tile - which
matters because the province is the march target and the render unit. Ben's call.

## Why it is worth doing beyond the tidy
The band's RESTING state is roughly 90% empty (NR-593) and it is the state the band is in most
of the time. A longer accordion does not fix that on its own, but it is the same surface and
the same pass, and the two should be settled together rather than in sequence.

## RULED (Ben, 2026-08-24, the Sprint 17b design form)
> Province rung: **Dissolve the rung.**

The repeat-click cycle loses its province stop. The cycle becomes battle, unit, building, tile - and the province is reached as a SECTION of the tile element, which is the clean reading of 'bundled into' and the one that makes the accordion worth building.

**The consequence, stated rather than discovered later.** The province is the march target and the render unit, and after this there is no gesture that selects a province WITHOUT also selecting a tile. That is acceptable because every tile carries its province in the accordion, so the province is never unreachable - but any code that assumed a province-only selection state (`ui_state::selected_province` set with `selected_entity` null) has to keep working when both are set. The march-order path is the one to check first.

`verify.select_province` writes exactly that province-only tuple, so the harness hook and the gesture will diverge after this. Either the hook follows the gesture, or the scripts that use it are testing a state a player can no longer reach.

BL-601.design:
## Ben's words
> "National borders should not diffuse together, instead they should borders extending their
> colour inwards. With this, we can drop the nation lens"

## The claim
A nation reads as a **bordered region**, not as a tinted field: the colour lives at the
boundary and falls off inwards, so two neighbours meeting never blend into a third colour
that belongs to neither. That is what makes the read always-on affordable - a border band
leaves the middle of a territory free for terrain, texture and whatever lens is active, which
a full-territory tint cannot do. Roads already work this way: drawn always, not behind a lens.

**So the Country lens dissolves rather than being deleted.** Its content becomes chrome.

## This overturns part of a designed item
BL-511 (province as render unit) is designed-and-unbuilt and specifies 'province-grain canvas
with **softened** borders'. Softening is the diffusion Ben is rejecting. The two cannot both
stand; newest-dated wins, so this item carries the border treatment and BL-511's remaining
content is the province-grain render, not its edge style.

## The call this needs
The Country lens is not only a wash - it is a **selection route**. LENSES.md's per-lens
routing table sends a hovered tile under that lens to its owning nation, and thence to the
Nation ledger. Dropping the lens removes the only path to a nation's ledger. Either the route
moves onto the always-on border (click a border, get the nation), or the nation ledger is
reached some other way. Ben's call, and it must be answered before the lens is removed rather
than after.

## RULED (Ben, 2026-08-24, the Sprint 17b design form)
> Nation ledger route: **Click the border itself.**

The always-on border band becomes the target. This is the answer that keeps the item coherent rather than bolting a replacement route somewhere else: the border is what now CARRIES the nation on screen, so it is the thing that should open it. A rail slot would have put a nation behind a menu while its territory sat under the pointer, and routing through the province card would have made the nation reachable only via a grain the player may not care about.

**What it needs.** A hit-test band along the border with real width - the drawn stroke is a line and a line is not clickable at play zoom - plus a hover read that says which nation before the click commits. It slots into LENSES.md's per-lens routing table as a lens-agnostic rule rather than a lens row, since the border is chrome now and not a lens.

This is also the first structure-grain selection in the shell, so it is the pattern BL-603 generalises. Build it as the general case, not as a nation special case.

BL-602.design:
## Ben's words
> "When we use lenses, for example 'Resource deposits' needs a selection element. This
> selection element for lenses should always fit in the header for the minimap, at the top
> right corner."

## There are two legend chromes today and one of them is invisible
LENSES.md documents both. **Count-driven keys** (Country, Market, Reach, Supply-routes) live
in the right chrome column above the minimap, collapsed by default. **Gradient-bar keys**
(Resource, Production, Scarcity, Population, Industry, Opportunity, Continent) are anchored
**flush-left of the minimap**, vertically centred on it - which is inside the rect the
always-open Selection band occupies.

Measured 2026-08-24 (NR-601): six of those seven are DRAWN AND BURIED. The Population key
renders 'Workforce efficiency / low ... high' and shows through the band as a ghost at roughly
a tenth of its contrast. Only the Continent key escapes, because it alone was moved to the
foreground draw list with an opaque fill (BL-376) - one of seven was fixed and the collision
was never generalised. Nothing had ever captured the other six to notice.

So this item is not only a tidy: **it is how six lenses get a readable key at all.**

## Provenance
This is the third dated ruling on the same region and it supersedes the earlier two.
BL-533 (legend in minimap quadrant) moved legends off the canvas into the right column;
BL-566 (legend inside minimap) revised that to put them INSIDE the minimap box with the full
width hosting the lens dropdown. Ben's 2026-08-24 wording - header, top right corner - is the
current one. The selector and the key share the home; one lens draws at most one key, so one
region serves all of them.

## Sequence
After the minimap and time-panel edge items, since both move the rect this region is measured
against.

mean. Removing them takes their `overlay_mode` values, their keys, their rows in LENSES.md's
roster, rung-applicability and selection-routing tables, and their entries in the action
dictionary. The lens-cycle modulus derives from the enum sentinel, so the bar re-numbers
itself without a hand-kept count.

## Two things to decide rather than assume
  * **Production has a Circumplanetary rung** - a per-body output-throughput badge - which is
    a different read from the planetary intensity tint and is not obviously covered by the
    same objection. Does it retire with the lens, or survive as body-level chrome?
  * **The ambient opportunity read** (BL-086) is a separate always-on cue, not this lens.
    Confirm it is untouched.

## Why this is cheap and why it is worth doing now
Every lens carries a permanent cost: a slot on the bar, a row in three tables, a key, and a
selection-routing rule that the structure-pivot item would otherwise have to answer for. Two
retirements shrink the surface the lens rebuild has to cover, so this lands BEFORE the pivot
work rather than after it.

BL-640.design: Design in POPULATION.md section Population demand and MARKETS.md section Demand channels. THE MEASURED CAUSE: population_demand's basket names food_rations, agricultural_produce, water, clean_water, consumer_goods, medical_supplies - and three of those six are made by NO ancient recipe, so a 0 CE campaign has three household goods. Recipes have carried an era field since BL-433; the demand baskets never did. THE WORK: band the basket the same way and author the ancient rows - ceramics, cloth, leather, dressed_stone - which are exactly the terminal artisan goods the ancient roster produces and nothing currently buys. Compose with the stratum ladder POPULATION.md already calls for: era decides WHICH value chain, stratum decides how far up it. This one item resurrects four of the seven ancient dead ends. SCOPE GREW, from BL-648's measurement (2026-08-26): this item also owns chain_depth's R1b list, and R1b hides a SECOND red list of the same defect class as the one BL-648 names. Neither inject_population_demand nor inject_background_demand is era-gated, so an ancient campaign genuinely 'wants' silicon, machinery, alloys and electronics - goods only the industrial arc can make - and R1b's hand-narrowed list quietly absorbs that. Banding the baskets is what makes R1b derivable from the injector registry instead of hand-maintained, so the two halves land together: band the demand, then let R1b read the banded truth. BL-648's agent deliberately did NOT fold this in, to avoid burying the ten goods that item exists to name - the right call, and it makes this item bigger than it looked when minted. THE MAGNITUDE, measured by BL-649's census (2026-08-26): at 0 CE, inject_background_demand alone is 8,417.8 of 10,544.0 total modelled market demand - 79.8% - and FIVE OF ITS SIX GOODS cannot be produced in that band at all. Household adds 435.4 more on clean_water / consumer_goods / medical_supplies, likewise unmakeable. So 65.7% OF ALL 0 CE DEMAND NAMES GOODS THE ANCIENT BAND CANNOT MAKE. That is not a rounding error in a basket, it is most of the demand in the world pointing at nothing, and it is why the ancient economy reads as having almost no buyers. Note the corollary for the tuning passes: fixing this will move prices everywhere, so the census must be run before and after and the deltas kept. MOVED INTO SPRINT 20 (Ben, 2026-08-26): these are the two levers that actually move spawn viability, and Sprint 20 owns the viability question through BL-634. Built in the same session as the diagnosis so the census and spawn_solvency baselines are hours old rather than a sprint stale.

BL-641.design: Design in FINANCE.md section Upkeep is credits AND goods - for buildings too. THE LARGEST STRUCTURAL SINK AVAILABLE, and it invents nothing: a unit already pays credits plus a goods vector through run_unit_upkeep, and a building pays credits only. That asymmetry is an omission, not a design. THE WORK: a per-building-type goods vector drawn against the owner's pool on the building's own body, in a fixed order (two buildings of one corp on one body draw the same stock and the order decides which goes short). The shortfall rule is the SAME rule - an unmet draw weakens the building by the same subtraction an out-of-supply unit takes; a factory short of tools runs badly, it does not vanish. Rates authored in economy.lua per building type, era-banded, every rate authorable at 0.0 so the SHAPE can land before the numbers are settled (the BL-454 precedent). Why it matters more than the others: demand then scales with how much industry exists, with no weight for anyone to maintain. MOVED INTO SPRINT 20 (Ben, 2026-08-26): these are the two levers that actually move spawn viability, and Sprint 20 owns the viability question through BL-634. Built in the same session as the diagnosis so the census and spawn_solvency baselines are hours old rather than a sprint stale. RATES STAY 0.0 UNTIL BL-654 LANDS (Ben, 2026-08-26). The measured collapse (227 -> 19 operating firms) is a consequence of drawing without bidding, not of the rate; BL-654's buy-with-a-ceiling is what makes a non-zero rate survivable, and the rate is then measured against the census and the operating-firm count rather than chosen.

BL-648.design: THE ITEM THAT STOPS THIS RECURRING, and it should land EARLY in the sprint rather than late. chain_depth's k_actor_consumed table lets a good pass the orphan check by NAMING a consumer, and ten goods currently name 'mercantile demand' - a mechanism grep says does not exist (market_clearing.cpp has exactly three injections: population, background, interbody). The guard has been green throughout. THE WORK: an exemption must name a pass that actually adds to a market's demand or draws from a pool, checked rather than asserted; the row FAILS when it cannot find one. Expect it to go red on ten goods the day it lands - that is the item working, and the rest of the sprint is what turns it green. Do NOT weaken it to pass in the meantime; a known-red guard with a named list is worth more than a green one that means nothing.

BL-649.design: THE INSTRUMENT THE SPRINT'S PASSES NEED, and the reason it is filed as its own item rather than as a row on another: 'did that change help' has no answer without a before. THE WORK: a harness reporting, per resource and per era band, the total modelled demand and the PASSES that inject it - so a good with no buyer is a row in a report rather than a discovery made three sprints later. Report, never assert a target: this is a measuring instrument, and the moment it asserts a number it starts being tuned against instead of read. It should be run BEFORE and AFTER each of the sprint's viability passes and the deltas kept. Per CLAUDE.md's 'tool creation is skill creation' it wants a verifier-headless entry, which needs Ben's permission. OWED ON LANDING: the verifier-headless skill entry, which needs Ben's permission. Invocation: cmd //c tools\verify\build_lua_harness.bat demand_census, then build_gen\verify\demand_census.exe [--seed N] [--ticks N] [--fast] [--band ancient|industrial|both].

BL-655.design: Ben's ruling on NR-679, 2026-08-26: KEEP BL-640's fix, and retune density back up toward the old world. The fix is not in question - Pass 6 was chasing ~90% of a demand that included goods the ancient band cannot produce, so it added firms against a gap that could never close, and correcting it took the world from 584 buildings / 104 corps to 261 / 64. TWO LEVERS REACH THE SAME COUNT AND THEY MEAN DIFFERENT THINGS, which is the whole of this item: (a) RAISE PASS 6'S TARGET FRACTION above 0.90 - the world then deliberately OVERPRODUCES, which means gluts, prices pinned at the floor, and thinner margins for everyone; it reaches the count without anyone wanting more. (b) RAISE THE DEMAND BASKETS - the world CONSUMES more per head, so more firms are supported at the same ~90% ratio and prices hold. TRY (b) FIRST: it preserves what BL-640 established, and POPULATION.md already names the knob as an open item - the cost of living, how much it costs a head to live, deliberately unquantified. (a) is the fallback and should be recorded as a deliberate oversupply if taken. MEASURE BOTH with demand_census against the committed baseline plus the corp and operating-building counts, and report the price consequence - a density that is right only because everything is worthless is not right.
